plugins.readme_text:
# dsh-go-game

圍棋 for the DeepSeek Harness. A full rules engine, a three-level AI partner,
a playout dead-stone estimator, optional LLM review, SGF save/load — surfaced
both as a DSH panel (`shell.overlay`) and as a standalone page at
`/dsh-go-game/`.

## What it does

**Rules (host half, pure JS).** 19×19 / 13×13 / 9×9, Chinese area scoring
(stones + surrounded empty points), configurable komi and handicap, capture by
liberty exhaustion, no suicide, simple ko (immediate recapture forbidden),
pass / two-pass end, resignation, unlimited undo, SGF import and export.
Dead-stone adjudication is explicit: both sides pass, dead stones are marked
(manually or by the estimator), then the area is counted.

**The AI.** Three levels, all run in the host process:

| level | how it plays |
| --- | --- |
| `easy` 入門 | random legal moves that avoid filling its own eyes |
| `medium` 中級 | greedy tactics: capture, rescue from atari, atari the opponent, shape/line preference |
| `hard` 進階 | the medium candidate list, each scored by light random playouts inside a wall-clock budget |

**Honest limit:** this is a practice partner, not an engine. On 19×19 even
`hard` is far below a human amateur; on 9×9 it plays a recognisable game.

**Dead-stone estimator.** `形勢判斷` runs random playouts (avoiding own-eye
fills) from the current position and reports which stones rarely survive, plus a
per-point ownership map the board renders as a translucent overlay. It is an
estimate, not an adjudication — correct anything it gets wrong with `標記死子`.

**LLM review (optional).** `覆盤` asks the harness `llm` service (no API keys in
this plugin) for a short Cantonese commentary plus a suggested move, which the
panel offers as a one-click play. Without a configured model it degrades to the
local scoring summary.

## Layout

| file | face | role |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `lib/engine.js` | shared | rules: board, capture, ko, score, SGF — no DOM, no DSH imports |
| `lib/ai.js` | host | heuristics, playout opponent, dead-stone estimator |
| `lib/gtp.js` | host | GTP bridge to an external neural-network engine (KataGo) |
| `lib/index.js` | host | sessions + every `/dsh-go-game/*` route, LLM review, SGF files |
| `lib/client.js` | web | the React panel registered in `shell.overlay` |
| `lib/page.html`, `lib/page.js` | web | the standalone page (a thin view over the same routes) |
| `cordis.patch.yml` | — | inserts the plugin row into the web profile roster |
| `test/*.test.mjs` | — | 98 cases: 26 engine, 11 AI, 22 host routes, 26 GTP, 13 engine fallback |
| `check-plugin.ps1` / `.cmd` | — | read-only install check |

No rules live in the browser: both views post intent and re-render the state the
host returns.

## Tests

```
node test/engine.test.mjs
node test/ai.test.mjs
node test/host.test.mjs
node test/gtp.test.mjs             # GTP bridge, driven by an injected fake engine
node test/engine-fallback.test.mjs # engine selected but absent -> built-in AI
node test/katago-live.mjs --root=<katago dir>   # real engine, skipped without --root
```

Run each file directly; `node --test` fails on this machine (the runner spawns a
piped child process and the sandbox rejects it). The host suite drives the real
routes through a mock webserver, mock `req`/`res` and a mock `llm`, so the whole
non-UI chain is covered offline.

## KataGo (optional neural-network opponent)

`lib/ai.js` is a heuristic/playout practice partner. For real strength,
`lib/gtp.js` drives an external KataGo process over GTP, **side by side** with the
built-in AI: the panel's `引擎` selector picks one per game, and a missing or
broken engine falls back to the built-in opponent automatically (the reason is
shown in the panel, not swallowed).

Layout it looks for (relative to the workspace, i.e. one level above the plugin):

```
katago/engine/katago.exe        Eigen (CPU) build, or any other backend
katago/engine/default_gtp.cfg   optional, ships with the release
katago/weights/*.bin.gz         one or more networks
```

Environment overrides:

| variable | default | meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `DSH_GO_GAME_KATAGO_ROOT` | `<plugin>/../../katago` | engine + weights root |
| `DSH_GO_GAME_KATAGO_THREADS` | 4 | search threads (stay below the core count) |
| `DSH_GO_GAME_KATAGO_VISITS` | 250 | hard visit ceiling per move |
| `DSH_GO_GAME_KATAGO_TIME` | 8 | **seconds per move** — bounds CPU latency |
| `DSH_GO_GAME_KATAGO_TIMEOUT` | 90000 | GTP command timeout (ms) |

`GET /dsh-go-game/engine` reports availability, the network list and live status;
`POST /dsh-go-game/engine {model:"<file>"}` switches network, restarting the
process (KataGo loads exactly one network at startup).

Measured on this machine — i5-8250U, 4 threads, no GPU, b18c384 on the AVX2 Eigen
build: first move ≈ 11 s (it loads the 93 MB network), later moves ≈ 8 s with
`maxTime=8`. Because the search is time-bounded, slower hardware loses strength
rather than latency. Every query replays the game onto a clean engine board after
an explicit `clear_board`: KataGo does *not* wipe the stones on a same-size
`boardsize`, which otherwise surfaces as a spurious "illegal move".

## Install (three steps, outside DSH)

The agent sandbox cannot write outside the workspace, so profile registration is
a manual step — run these in a normal terminal:

1. In the active profile `package.json` (`%APPDATA%\dsh-desktop\harness\profiles\web`):
   add `"dsh-go-game": "link:C:/AppDev/DSH_WORKSPACE/dsh-go-game"` to
   `dependencies`, and append `"dsh-go-game"` to `dsh.profile.bundles`.
2. Point node_modules at the source directory (DSH does not run `pnpm install`
   on boot, and a missing link fails silently):

   ```
   mklink /J "%APPDATA%\dsh-desktop\harness\profiles\web\node_modules\dsh-go-game" "C:\AppDev\DSH_WORKSPACE\dsh-go-game"
   ```

3. Restart DSH.

`check-plugin.cmd` verifies all four links of the chain (package → registration →
node_modules → live route) at any point.

Routes are unauthenticated on loopback, matching the other local plugins:
`GET /dsh-go-game/status` answering JSON is the fastest proof of life.

## Notes and unverified parts

- Sessions live in host memory (12-hour idle sweep) and are keyed by a client id
  the panel/page generates; restarting DSH clears them. SGF files persist under
  `<workspace>/.dsh-go-game/games/`.
- The playout estimator is CPU-bound by design and budget-limited (default
  1500 ms, 40 playouts). It runs on the host so the panel never blocks.
- **Not yet verified on a live GUI**: the panel's rendering inside
  `shell.overlay`, its pointer-event behaviour, and the LLM review path against a
  real provider. The engine, AI and every route are covered by the offline
  suites.

# rulemux > One set of rules, **one source of truth**: edit once, and it reaches **every agent in every > workspace**. > Same effect and same token cost as writing `AGENTS.md` by hand — **never fades out, never accumulates, no symlinks, free to add and remove files**. [中文版](README.zh-CN.md) | [Design docs](docs/design/architecture.md) --- ## 1. What is this ### 1.1 The pain - **Every agent keeps rules somewhere else**: `.codebuddy/rules/`, `.trae/rules/`, a single `AGENTS.md`, an injected recall block… one coding convention has to be rewritten once per agent. - **And every workspace keeps its own copy**: to make a rule apply in a workspace you write it there again. - So the rules that are genuinely **shared** (team conventions, coding standards) can neither be factored out nor maintained: one sentence means opening *agents × workspaces* files, with no guarantee you did not miss one. ### 1.2 What rulemux does You maintain **one source of truth**: a set of rule documents you wrote, declared in `~/.rulemux/config.toml` as the tree below. `rulemux sync` copies them — really copies — into each agent's **native rules directory**. Upper layers are inherited by the ones below them, so **one edit reaches every agent in every workspace on the next sync**. ``` One source of truth (your own .md files, declared in ~/.rulemux/config.toml) │ ├─ Layer 1 · org-wide rules ─────────────► every agent × every workspace │ │ │ ├─ Layer 2 · dev rules │ │ ├─ Layer 3 · mini-app rules │ │ │ └─ … │ │ ├─ Layer 3 · backend rules │ │ │ └─ … │ │ └─ Layer 3 · client-side rules │ │ └─ … │ │ │ └─ Layer 2 · non-dev rules │ └─ Layer 3 · workspace daily rules … │ └─ … │ └─ Layer 4 · one workspace's own rules ──► only in that workspace rulemux sync ↓ real copies (never fades out / never accumulates / no symlinks) workspace A ──► .codebuddy/rules/ .trae/rules/ (dsh: injected, nothing on disk) workspace B ──► .codebuddy/rules/ .trae/rules/ (dsh: injected, nothing on disk) ``` - **Rules are reused**: layer 3 inherits layer 2, layer 2 inherits layer 1 — write what is shared once, and get more specific as you go down. - **Layers fan out**: each layer declares which agents and which workspaces it applies to; no file is duplicated per combination. - **Edit once, applies everywhere**: change a sentence up top and every workspace and agent that inherits it is aligned on the next sync. - **No depth limit**: the `…` under layer 3 is a padding layer — `use` is expanded **recursively**, so you can nest as deep as you like. The only thing not allowed is a **cycle** (A uses B and B uses A), which fails at config load. The tree is built with `use` on `[[file_group]]` (inherit the layer above) plus `workspace` on `[[source]]` (where it lands): ```toml [[file_group]] name = "base" # layer 1: org-wide path = ["/rules/00-base.md"] [[file_group]] name = "dev" # layer 2: dev rules use = ["base"] # inherits layer 1 path = ["/rules/10-dev.md"] [[file_group]] name = "miniapp" # layer 3: mini-app rules use = ["dev"] # inherits layer 2 (and therefore layer 1) path = ["/rules/20-miniapp.md"] [[source]] groups = ["miniapp"] # lands as base + dev + miniapp workspace = ["/work/miniapp-a", "/work/miniapp-b"] [[source]] path = ["/rules/proj-x-only.md"] # layer 4: this workspace only workspace = ["/work/proj-x"] ``` See §5.2 for the full grouping and matching syntax. ### 1.3 The invariants - **rulemux does not own or maintain any rule content**: your source files stay yours — rulemux only delivers them. Which agents / workspaces they apply to is declared in your config. - **The session hook is (almost) only the courier.** Rule *content* is never injected: files are really copied into the directory the agent loads natively, so they enjoy static-prefix semantics (never fade out mid-conversation, never accumulate). The single, deliberate exception is one **transient notice line** the hook emits when it detects that the rules really changed — it asks you to start a new session. See §5.3. - **No symlinks, free add/remove**: real copies only; delete a source from the config and its copy disappears on the next sync. > Why not "just inject with a hook"? Hook injection lands in the dynamic part of the context: it > gets summarised away on compaction (fades out) or re-appended every turn (token blow-up). > See [design/architecture.md](docs/design/architecture.md) §一. --- ## 2. Supported scope rulemux ships **one adapter per agent**, and an adapter is only installable once its rules directory and hook location have been confirmed by a real canary test. Today: | Agent | Tier | Rules directory | Skills directory | Status | |---|---|---|---|---| | **codebuddy** | Tier-1 (real copy) | `.codebuddy/rules/`; user-level `~/.codebuddy/rules/` | `.codebuddy/skills/`; user-level `~/.codebuddy/skills/` + `~/.workbuddy/skills/` (both written) | ✅ **Verified — installable** (`codebuddy-cn` is an alias) | | **workbuddy** | Tier-1 (real copy) | `.codebuddy/rules/` (**shared** with codebuddy, canary-proven 2026-10-09) | `.codebuddy/skills/` (shared with codebuddy); user-level: both dirs written as above | ✅ **Verified — installable** (separate app: own `~/.workbuddy/settings.json` hook, no longer an alias of codebuddy) | | claude (Claude Code) | Tier-1 | `.claude/rules/` | not yet | ⚠️ registered, **not verified yet** — cannot be installed | | **trae** (Trae CN) | Tier-1 (real copy) | `.trae/rules/` | `.trae/skills/` (workspace, 🔴 pending canary); user-level `~/.trae-cn/skills/` (verified) | ✅ **Verified — installable** (2026-10-09 canary: user-level hook `~/.trae-cn/hooks.json`; the international `~/.trae` build is not wired yet) | | codex | Tier-2 (injection) | none — injects into context | not yet | ⚠️ registered, **not verified yet** | | opencode | Tier-2 (injection) | none — injects into context | not yet | ⚠️ registered, **not verified yet** | | **dsh** (DeepSeek Harness) | Tier-2 (injection) | none — injects into context | `.dsh/skills/`; user-level `~/.dsh/skills/` | ✅ **Verified — installable**; rules are delivered by a **separate dsh plugin** — install it with `dsh plugin --profile

add rulemux-dsh` (rulemux only renders the text with `inject`, and writes nothing into your workspace for rules). Skills are real copies into the native skills dirs, synced by the same plugin at session start (source-verified 2026-10-14 against `deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness`, verified on a real dsh 2026-10-15) | - `rulemux init` **refuses** any agent that is not verified — it will not half-install an adapter whose behaviour has not been proven. `rulemux doctor` marks unverified agents with ⚠. - **Skill injection (shipped 2026-10-12, codebuddy / workbuddy; dsh added 2026-10-14)**: declare local skill directories with `[[skill_source]]`; they are really copied into the agent's native skills directory (as `__rulemux__/` — your own skills are never touched). With `scope = "user"` they land in the **user-level (global)** directories. Rules and skills both support the dual scope; see §5.4. claude / codex / opencode do not take skills yet; trae takes skills (CN: workspace `.trae/skills` + user-level `~/.trae-cn/skills`, workspace pending canary). - **Tier-2 is a deliberate downgrade** for agents that have no rules directory (they only read a single `AGENTS.md`). It injects via the session hook and never touches your own `AGENTS.md`, but it cannot satisfy the "never fades out" bar. See [design/features/hook-injection.md](docs/design/features/hook-injection.md). - **dsh is plugin-delivered: for rules nothing lands on disk, for skills real copies land in `.dsh/skills/`**: it has no hook file and no rules directory, so rulemux never writes into your workspace for rules. A **separate plugin package** in this repo ([`dsh-plugin/`](dsh-plugin/)) — on npm as `rulemux-dsh` — asks the CLI for the rules rendered for the session's workspace (`rulemux inject --agent

plugins.description: DSH 嵌入式硬件沙盒插件：3D 装配协作感知 + 项目级硬件在环仿真
plugins.readme_text: Web profile plugin — host half + browser half. > **English**: [README.md](README.md) | **中文**: [README.zh.md](README.zh.md) --- # DSH Hardware Sandbox **A 3D hardware sandbox for DSH: build the assembly, wire it up, and run your project's own code against virtual hardware.** **Install (from GitHub; this package is not published on npm)** ```sh dsh plugin --profile web add github:Noob-stupid/dsh-breadboard ``` Then reload the page. The sandbox registers into the **`main`** slot (the 3D view) and the **`sidebar.panellist`** slot (the panels); `skill/SKILL.md` ships with the plugin, so an agent that has it installed already knows how to drive it. **Like it?** Open this plugin's page in the Plugins manager — its own bottom-right corner carries a small, plain-text link to [give it a star on GitHub](https://github.com/Noob-stupid/dsh-breadboard). It is one transparent line, no box, no banner, and it only ever appears on this plugin's page. Three things make that one line work — all three are in this repository: | Requirement | Where | Note | |---|---|---| | repo topic `dsh-plugin` | GitHub repository topics | makes the repo discoverable in community lists | | a `dsh.bundle` manifest | `package.json` → `"dsh": { "bundle": { "patch": "./cordis.patch.yml" } }` | **without it `dsh plugin add` installs nothing** — and the UI symptom is misleading: the plugin list says "no composition bundle declared", while what actually broke is the assembly, so every `/api/*` returns 404 and the panel simply never appears | | an exported `apply(ctx)` | `src/index.ts` (host) / `src/client/index.ts` (browser) | host half registers routes, tools and the simulation engine; browser half registers the two slots above | ## What it is / what it solves Normally the parts of a hardware project you can only *try on the real board* are the wiring itself, the sensor semantics at register level, and the failure handling. This plugin moves those into a virtual scene that actually runs: - **3D assembly** — drop parts from the built-in model library (ESP32, Raspberry Pi 4B, BME280, HC-SR501 PIR, LED module, MPL3115A2, breadboard), wire them port by port, and get a live SSOT (single source of truth) assembly state with topology and electrical checks. - **Project-level hardware-in-the-loop** — a **real Python process** runs **your project's code**. A Python shim intercepts its `smbus`/I2C access and answers from virtual devices, so the project under test reads register-level values (e.g. it performs the real BME280 compensation math on data coming from the virtual chip). - **Networked-device emulation** (a second, separate class of virtual hardware) — a device that actively POSTs to **your** external HTTP backend on a real cadence: register → pull config → periodic report. Verified end-to-end against a real seat-selection system (device → HTTP → backend state machine → database). - **Failure injection** — unplug a wire, return NACK, force a reading, take a device offline, and watch whether the project's error handling actually catches it. - **Project-level convenience** — scan a real project folder to learn which hardware it needs, and switch the entire hardware setup in one click. Requires DSH with the **`web`** profile and `webServer`, `tools` and `subprocess` services. The host half declares them as **hard `inject` dependencies on purpose**: if any of them is missing the plugin does not activate at all, rather than activating with tools silently unregistered, a blank panel, or a simulation engine that cannot spawn. ### See it without a real project `examples/zhizuo-virtual-esp32/` is a standalone script version of the virtual ESP32 seat sensor. `hw_list_projects` lists the built-in demo project (**zhizuo-seat-node**) together with whether it is currently wired end to end; `hw_import_project` puts its parts, wires and network binding in place in one call. ## UI tour The interface is currently **Chinese only** — the labels below are the literal ones on screen. | Panel | What it does | |---|---| | **③ Project (one-click hardware swap)** | the main workflow. Per project body: file count (`N files (M skipped while sampling)` when sampling skipped files), **Scan requirements**, **Delete**; plus **+ Import project body (pick folder)** and **+ Import model bundle (pick folder)** | | **① Add component** | click a model key to drop it into the scene (collapsed by default) | | **② Re-skin models** | search for a model / import a file, and re-skin one of the model keys above; a model key with no geometry renders as a placeholder box (collapsed by default) | | **Statistics** | render statistics (draw calls / triangles / FPS) — pure read, off by default | | **Center 3D view** | placed components with world transforms, **blue cables** between ports, spatial warning boxes drawn on the components that have `warn`/`error` warnings, gizmo/right-click menu (pin, delete), port tooltips | | **Panel overlay input box** | send a message to the current session without leaving the panel; if the host exposes no `agents` service the box is hidden (`capabilities.chat` is absent) | Two of those deserve emphasis: - **Scan requirements is a UI button only.** It is not exposed as an agent tool — the agent side has no equivalent. What the agent *can* do is everything after that: place parts, wire them, build a project blueprint, run simulations. - **Deleting a project only deletes the project definition** (that one JSON). It does **not** touch the scene, so removing a project never wipes the hardware you have on screen. ## Quick start: three steps 1. **Import the project body** — *+ Import project body (pick folder)*, point it at a **complete project folder** (frontend + backend + hardware code). It is imported **without** models; the host reads it to work out which hardware it needs. 2. **Scan what hardware it needs** — the **Scan requirements** button in the ③ panel (UI only, see above). The report lists each candidate model key with the **evidence** — which files it was seen in — so you can judge it yourself; when the scan had to sample, it says so instead of implying it read everything. 3. **Import a model bundle** — *+ Import model bundle (pick folder)*, a folder laid out as `/model.glb`. Whatever you skip keeps rendering as a placeholder box. Or skip steps 1–3 entirely: describe the system to the agent and let it call **`hw_save_project`** to write a blueprint, then **`hw_import_project`** to place every part, wire and network binding in one go. ## Agent tools: 16 `hw_*` tools This is the actual registered list (nothing added, nothing omitted). The **when to use** column is the point of the table: these tools are not interchangeable. ### Projects | Tool | What it does | When to use it | |---|---|---| | `hw_list_projects` | list built-in hardware projects: parts, wires, network config, and whether each is currently wired end to end | **before** hand-placing anything — a blueprint is one call, hand-assembly is four steps and a missed step fails silently | | `hw_import_project` | import a project: **clears the current assembly first**, then places parts, wires and network bindings | switching the whole hardware set; note it *replaces*, it does not add | | `hw_save_project` | create or overwrite a project blueprint (stored under `$DSH_HOME/dsh-hardware-sandbox/projects/`) | the user described a system in words — write it down as a blueprint, then import it | ### Assembly | Tool | What it does | When to use it | |---|---|---| | `hw_get_assembly` | read the SSOT summary: revision, components, connections, warnings (with their `message`, not just the code), power summary, virtual devices | **before every edit** — you need the real port ids; port ids are pin identities (`E4`), not silkscreen names (`GPIO23`) | | `hw_edit_assembly` | one tool over the contract's `ClientAction` union: place / move / rotate / connect / disconnect / remove / pin | any change to the scene. It takes an action object, so read the samples

plugins.description: DSH plugin: pin the no-context fallback Workspace of new Sessions to one fixed folder (browser-side uiWorkspace policy, no host code).
plugins.readme_text:
# dsh-plugin-default-workspace

A small DSH plugin that pins the **no-context fallback Workspace of new
Sessions** to one folder, chosen in the Settings dialog.

## Why this exists

DSH chooses the Workspace of a new Session from context, never from
configuration:

| Situation | Stock DSH behavior | With this plugin |
|---|---|---|
| A Session holding a conversation is open in some folder | the new Session stays in that folder | unchanged |
| The app opens on a saved Session holding a conversation | that Session is restored | unchanged |
| An explicit target is passed (a workspace row's **+**, *add workspace*) | that target is used | unchanged |
| **Nothing to go on**: no saved selection, a saved Session that no longer exists, or a saved/current **empty New Session** (nothing ever sent) | the *most recently active* Workspace | **the folder chosen in Settings** |
| **The Session you are viewing is archived** | the main selection is cleared and the app drops to its *choose a Workspace* hero | **a new Session in that Session's own Workspace**, or the chosen folder when it had no Workspace |

An empty New Session is not "already conversing in another folder": DSH marks a
Session `blank` (`SessionSummary.blank`) until its first turn starts, and that
flag is what decides the last-but-one row above. Clicking a workspace row and
typing still starts the conversation in that folder; the folder only takes over
once there is a conversation in it.

Archiving is the one case where the folder that comes back is *not* the chosen
one: the conversation is gone but the project is not, so archiving a Session in
`D:\CodeProjects\Moltenfrost` leaves you in `Moltenfrost` with a fresh New
Session. A Session that belonged to no Workspace has no folder of its own to
keep, so it falls back to the chosen folder — the same rule as the row above.
Only clearing a main Session is honoured this way; archiving any other row
navigates nothing, exactly as before.

The Host owns no setting for this. The only "default workspace" concept in DSH
(`workspaceRegistry.initializeDefault`, `<Documents>\deepseek-harness\default-workspace`)
is created once on a pristine install and requires an empty Workspace registry
*and* empty Session history, so it cannot be repointed on an installation that
already has Sessions.

## Choosing the folder

Settings carries one page from this plugin, **Default folder**, as its own
navigation tab (`settings.section`, order 30 — after the shipped sections):

- the selector lists every registered Workspace by path, plus **Follow DSH**,
  which switches the plugin off and restores the stock "most recently active
  Workspace" rule;
- **Choose another folder…** opens the same folder chooser the Workspace UI
  uses — the Desktop preload dialog when the shell exposes it, otherwise the
  Host chooser through `uiWorkspace.pickDirectory()`. A folder the Workspace
  registry does not know yet is registered first, exactly like
  **Add workspace…** (`uiWorkspace.workspaces.create({ path })`), so a picked
  folder is immediately usable;
- the choice is stored in the page's localStorage under
  `dsh.default-workspace.settings` and is read at every routing decision, so it
  applies to the next New Session with no reload and no re-apply.

With nothing stored, the compiled-in `DEFAULT_WORKSPACE_PATH` still applies, so
an installation that never opens the page behaves exactly as it did before. A
stored folder that is not registered has no effect and the stock rule stays in
charge — this plugin never invents a Workspace.

The preference lives in the browser, not in the Host user-settings document: the
policy this plugin installs is browser-side, and a Host-backed field would make
the host half depend on the framework's schema package, which a plugin mounted
from a bare `file:///…` path cannot resolve. See *Why localStorage* below.

## Files

| Path | Role |
|---|---|
| `package.json` | Package manifest: host half plus the `dsh.client` declaration and `exports["./client"]` the Client module system scans |
| `lib/index.js` | Host half — deliberately empty; the policy and its Settings page are browser-side |
| `lib/client.js` | Browser half — wraps `uiWorkspace.startSession`, `uiWorkspace.restoreSelection`, and `uiWorkspace.clearMain`, and contributes the **Default folder** Settings page |
| `test/interception.test.mjs` | Maintenance check: runs the real browser bundle against a fake `uiWorkspace` and asserts every rule above, the Settings page included |
| `test/host-integration.test.mjs` | Maintenance check: asks the running Host whether it composes and serves this plugin's browser half |
| `test/probe-report.mjs` | Reads the decision trace the browser half writes into the page's localStorage |
| `CHANGELOG.md` | Release notes |
| `LICENSE` | MIT |

The browser half wraps three navigation entry points on the `uiWorkspace`
service instance. The two navigation wrappers delegate to the stock method for
every case they do not own; the third wraps the clear that ends an archive.
Every wrapper swallows its own failures back into the stock flow, so the worst
case is exactly the stock behavior.

### Why localStorage

The Host settings document edits fields a plugin declares with `.volatile()` in
its exported `Config` schema, which comes from `@deepseek-ai/schemastery`. A
plugin mounted as a `file:///…` Loader row resolves its own imports relative to
its directory, so that bare specifier is unreachable without shipping a
`node_modules` next to the plugin. The preference is therefore browser-local,
which is also where the policy lives. The cost is that it is per browser origin
and invisible to the Host configuration file; the benefit is a plugin with no
dependencies at all.

## Four constraints this plugin had to learn the hard way

Each one was learned against the live app rather than from documentation; the
traces from `test/probe-report.mjs` are what pinned them down.

1. **Declare no `inject`.** With `inject: ["uiWorkspace"]` the plugin never
   applied at all — no error, no console line, just a page where the policy did
   not exist. The service does not exist yet when the entry is applied
   (the trace shows `apply` → `waiting` → installed 247 ms later), so the
   browser half polls `ctx.get("uiWorkspace")` every 50 ms instead of waiting.
2. **Never read another plugin's services through a context proxy.** The stock
   bootstrap builds its supersession signal with
   `this.ctx.layout.beginNavigation()`; doing that from here throws
   `cannot get property "layout" without inject` — which made the primary path
   fall back to the stock flow. Supersession is now checked against
   `mainReference`, and `test/interception.test.mjs` runs against a service whose
   `ctx` has no `layout` at all, so this cannot regress unnoticed.
3. **`blank`, not "exists", decides.** A saved Session that still exists but
   never received a turn is an empty New Session, and must not pin its folder.
   DSH's `SessionSummary.blank` carries exactly that fact.
4. **The boot watcher is one-shot, and archiving is not a navigation entry
   point.** `uiWorkspace.watchNavigation` restores a selection exactly once, at
   startup; afterwards it only watches for one thing — a main Session that has
   become archived — and its reaction to that is `clearMain()`, which drops the
   main reference *and* the persisted selection and leaves the stock hero
   standing. Wrapping `startSession` and `restoreSelection` therefore misses
   archiving completely, and a page that archives its main Session sits on
   "choose a Workspace" until the user navigates by hand. The trace proves it:
   the two `startSession` decisions that recovered the app are 20 seconds apart,
   with nothing at all recorded in between. `clearMain` is the only choke point
   every archive route passes through — the row action, the shortcut, the
   stop-and-archive dialog, another plugin, and the watcher's own
   `clearArchivedCurrent` — so that is what gets wrapped, and it reads the
   Session's Workspace *before* delegating, because the clear is what erases the
   identity that names it.

## Mounting

The plugin is mounted by one patch in the profi

plugins.description: One-click restart for the DeepSeek Harness desktop app: a sidebar-footer button plus a detached supervisor that relaunches the whole app, so a rebuilt plugin or profile change takes effect immediately.
plugins.readme_text:
# dsh-plugin-restart · 一键重启 DSH

[![CI](https://github.com/SOH4C4759/dsh-plugin-restart/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/SOH4C4759/dsh-plugin-restart/actions/workflows/ci.yml)
[![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-blue.svg)](LICENSE)

> English: [README.en.md](README.en.md)

插件迭代后，**点一下界面上的「重启 DSH」按钮**，整个 DeepSeek Harness 桌面应用（Electron 外壳 + Host）会退出并自动重新启动，让刚重建的插件包、组合（bundle）、preset 立即生效。

- **按钮位置可配置**（`position`，5 个预设）：侧栏页脚（默认）、会话标题栏、输入框工具行、输入框下方、不显示按钮。位置既写在 profile patch 里，也能在**「设置 → 插件 → 一键重启 DSH」这一页**直接改，改完即时生效、不需要重启。
- **回复末尾的自动提示**：Host 发现**已加载的 Host 入口模块被重写**（只有重启能换掉那一代代码）时才记一个待重启标记；下一轮回复结束时，提示卡直接出现在**这条回复的末尾**（`conversation.chat.turnTail`——DSH 给「完成的一轮回复、动作行之前」的原生席位），一句标题、两个按钮：`稍后` / `立即重启`。它只出现在**最新一轮**上，不会把整段历史都刷一遍；`稍后` 只收起本次，下次真正的重建会再出现。装插件、启停插件、改 patch 都是 DSH **当场生效**的，不会提示。
- 默认位置是**左下角头像/设置那一排**的图标按钮（`sidebar.footer.action`，`order: 10`）：纯图标、无文字，悬停有提示，点击后在**侧栏内**（不是窗口角落）弹出确认面板——一句标题 `重启 DSH`、一条弱化的范围备注 `（应用与 Host）`，加 取消 / 立即重启。
- 可选：`tray/tray-host.ps1` 提供 Windows 托盘入口「重启 DSH」，不依赖界面也能重启/拉起。

本包**不修改 DSH 源码、不需要 fork**：它是一个标准 profile bundle（`dsh.bundle.patch` + `dsh.client`），装进当前 profile 即可。

## 视频

分 P 讲解（B 站）：[【工具演示】一键重启 DSH](https://www.bilibili.com/video/BV1qxpA6aE1X/)

- **P1** 装完插件，点一下就知道生效了没有（v1.0 的原始讲解）
- **P2** v1.1.0 · 总览：不用再自己记着重启
- **P3** v1.1.0 · 回复末尾的自动提示
- **P4** v1.1.0 · 按钮位置可配置

片子里的画面都是这台机器上运行中的应用截图，不是示意图。

## 环境要求

| 项 | 要求 | 为什么 |
|---|---|---|
| 操作系统 | Windows 10 / 11 | 守护脚本用 `Get-Process` / `Start-Process` / `taskkill` / WMI `Win32_Process.Create`，均为 Windows 专有 |
| Shell | **Windows PowerShell 5.1**（`powershell.exe`） | `lib/restart-supervisor.ps1` 声明 `#requires -Version 5.1`；Host 默认就以 `powershell.exe` 启动守护脚本（可用 `DSH_POWERSHELL` 覆盖）。**未适配 pwsh 7** |
| Node | ≥ 20（仅用于自检脚本） | 插件本体在 DSH 内运行，不需要额外的 Node 运行时 |
| DSH | 桌面版（Electron 外壳） | 一键重启的对象是「应用 + Host」，纯 Web/CLI 形态没有可重启的外壳 |

`package.json` 里声明了 `"os": ["win32"]`，在其它平台上安装会被包管理器直接拒绝。

## 为什么必须这么做（进程模型约束）

| 事实 | 后果 |
|---|---|
| 桌面端 Host 是 Electron 主进程的子进程，主进程把 Host 的退出一律当作崩溃（`dsh desktop host stopped`），并弹出原生对话框「DeepSeek Harness 无法使用」+ Windows 系统提示音 | 「只重启 Host」必然弹框；**杀进程的顺序也必须先杀 Electron 主进程**（见第 6 节），否则每次一键重启都会闪一个对话框 |
| 官方菜单里的「重启应用与 Host」被编译在 `development` 开关后面（正式版构建不暴露） | 界面/菜单没有可用重启入口 |
| Host 进程无法让父进程 `app.relaunch()`，也无法在自身被拆掉后继续干活 | 需要**脱离进程的守护者** |

### Windows 上「脱离进程」的实测结论（都踩过坑，改动前先读）

1. **`spawn(exe, args, { detached: true, stdio: 'ignore' })` 不足以让子进程在父进程退出后存活。**
   实测：父进程退出后，detached 子进程的标记文件**从未生成**；同样内容经 `cmd /c start` 启动则生成。早期版本的守护脚本因此「杀掉了旧应用，却没能启动新应用」——日志停在 `processes after stop = 0` 之后。
2. **`cmd /c start` 一旦 stdout 被捕获就会永久阻塞。** 实测：裸调用 35ms 返回；`| Out-Null` 或 `| ForEach-Object` 下无限挂起（`start` 不退出，管道等不到 EOF）。
3. 因此守护进程改用 **WMI 创建**（`Win32_Process.Create`）：由 WMI 服务在**本进程树与句柄继承之外**创建，调用立即返回。实现见 `index.js` 的 `spawnSupervisor`（命令行经 base64 临时文件传递，避免 `-Command` 吞引号）。
4. **拉起 GUI 应用用 `Start-Process`，并且要等窗口，而不是只等进程。**
   实测：在隐藏控制台里启动应用，进程起来了但**没有可见窗口**——用户看到的就是「客户端没被拉起」。守护脚本现在轮询 `MainWindowHandle`：拿到窗口才算 `phase: relaunched`；20 秒内没窗口则记为 `relaunched-no-window`（诚实反映异常，而不是谎报成功）。

守护脚本（`lib/restart-supervisor.ps1`）的顺序：等待触发 → **先校验 exe 存在**（绝不关闭一个无法重新启动的应用）→ 列出将要终止的进程 → **先单独终止应用根进程（Electron 主进程）并确认它已消失** → 再按镜像名 `taskkill /F` 处理其余进程 → 有界等待到全部消失 → 启动**恰好一个**实例 → 等窗口 → 写 `restart-result.json`（无 BOM，Node 的 `JSON.parse` 才能读）。

> 关于「等待」：HTTP 应答与守护脚本启动之间的延迟 `armDelayMs` 由 **Host 侧** `setTimeout` 完成（`index.js` 的 `apply()`），不通过命令行传给守护脚本——守护脚本多等一秒就会被用户感知成「点了没反应」。`spawnSupervisor` 只传 `-Exe / -GraceMs / -StateDir / -LogPath / -ResultPath`。

### 5. 守护进程的控制台窗口必须在创建时就隐藏

WMI 创建的进程会**分配一个新的控制台**。命令行里的 `-WindowStyle Hidden` 是 PowerShell 启动**之后**才生效的，所以窗口会先以可见状态创建、再被隐藏——用户看到的就是每次重启动一下的命令行窗口。做法是给 `Win32_Process.Create` 传一个 `Win32_ProcessStartup` 并把 `ShowWindow` 设为 `0`（SW_HIDE），让控制台**创建时就是隐藏的**。

实测边界（Windows 11 + PowerShell 5.1）：

| 做法 | 控制台可见 | 进程是否正常执行 |
|---|---|---|
| 不传 startup info | **可见** | 是 |
| 命令行 `-WindowStyle Hidden` | 隐藏（但创建瞬间会闪） | 是 |
| **`ShowWindow = 0`** | **隐藏，且无闪窗** | 是 |
| `ShowWindow = 0` + `CreateFlags = 1` | — | **否：进程起来了但从不执行载荷** |
| `ShowWindow = 0` + `CreateFlags = 0x08000000` | — | 否：`Create` 返回 21（参数错误） |

所以**不要**设 `CreateFlags`。另外 `Invoke-CimMethod -ClassName Win32_Process` 无法封送内嵌的 `Win32_ProcessStartup` 对象（报「类型不匹配」），必须走经典 `[wmiclass]'Win32_Process'` 路径。`tests/selfcheck.mjs` 与 `tests/host-arm-e2e.ps1` 都固化了这几条，防止回退。

### 6. 停止顺序必须先杀 Electron 主进程，否则每次都闪一个 Windows 对话框

**现象**：一键重启时会短暂闪出一个白色 Windows 对话框，同时响一声系统提示音。用探针（窗口截图 + 读子控件文字 + WASAPI 分进程声音归因）抓到的是：

```
243185 / 243496  taskkill   逐个杀应用进程
243726  NEW-WINDOW  #32770  «DeepSeek Harness 无法使用»
243818  CAPTURE     标题「DeepSeek Harness 无法使用」正文「应用无法启动或已意外停止。」
                    按钮：退出 / 重启 / 禁用第三方插件、备份 profile patch 并重启
243912  SOUND       pid=0（Windows 系统声音会话）peak=0.1372
```

**原因**：Electron 主进程把 Host 当作自己的孩子监视。守护脚本原来按 `Get-Process` 的返回顺序（PID 升序）逐个 `taskkill`，而 **PID 会被回收，Host 完全可能排在主进程前面**。Host 先死、主进程还活着的那个瞬间，主进程就走「desktop host stopped」的错误处理，弹出上面这个原生框并播放系统音；紧接着主进程自己也被下一个 `taskkill` 杀掉，所以用户只看到「一闪」。

这也是它偶发的原因：主进程恰好先被杀的那几次重启，什么都不会出现。

**做法**：用 `Win32_Process` 的 `ParentProcessId` 建父子映射，找出**应用根进程**（其余应用进程的祖先，即 Electron 主进程），**单独**先 `taskkill /F`，再用 `Wait-AppProcessGone` 轮询确认它真的消失，之后才动其余进程。父映射拿不到时退化为「最早启动的那个进程」——主进程永远是应用树里最先创建的。`tray/tray-functions.ps1` 的 `Stop-ProcessTree` 走同一套逻辑（托盘路径同样会踩这个坑）。

> 为什么不直接用 Host 传进来的 `targetPid`：进程检测失败时它可能就是 Host 自己，按它先杀等于把 bug 装回去；用 OS 的父子关系判断是自洽的，两条入口都适用。`tests/supervisor-e2e.ps1`（case 4）与 `tests/tray-selfcheck.ps1` 都用「父进程 + 同镜像名子进程」复现了这个树形并锁住顺序。

## 安装

```powershell
# 在 DSH 里（推荐）：plugin_manager install_bundle，target = 本目录绝对路径
# 或走桌面端自带 CLI carrier：
$dsh = "$env:LOCALAPPDATA\Programs\DeepSeek Harness\resources\runtime\cli\bin\dsh.cmd"
& $dsh plugin --profile desktop add "<你克隆这个仓库的路径>"
```

### 唯一一次人工引导（之后不再需要）

安装后：

- **客户端半（按钮）立即生效**：`sidebar.footer.action` 里会出现 `ui-dsh-restart / dsh-restart`（可用 `cordis_inspect_query` 的 Client `Slots` 确认）。
- **Host 半（重启路由）需要一次应用重启才加载**。三条实测结论，都不要再试：
  1. **Host 半不能热重载**。`plugin_manager set_plugin` 能干净地注销/重挂这一行（路由随禁用消失、启用后回来），但进程内的 ESM 模块缓存会一直交出**第一次 import 的那份代码**。实测：改完磁盘上的 `index.js` 后反复「禁用→启用」，报错栈的行号与文件内容始终是旧版本。
  2. **改包版本也无效**。把 `version` 从 1.0.0 提到 1.0.1 再 `install_bundle`，只会得到 `ambiguous-install`；模块缓存按解析出的标识符缓存，与版本无关。
  3. **profile 里的 `dsh-hmr` 只监视 profile 自身**（`baseDir` = profile 目录），不监视被 `link:` 进来的外部插件目录，所以改外部包也不会触发重载。

  因此请**手动关闭并重新打开 DeepSeek Harness 一次**（托盘 → 退出，或关闭窗口后重新打开）。此后每次插件迭代都只需点按钮。

> **一次教训**：Host 半第一次激活失败时，失败会被这一代进程记住（`fiberPhase: failed`），而磁盘上的修复无法生效——缓存里是旧代码。这一轮就是这样暴露并修掉了两个真实缺陷（cordis 在未 `inject` 时访问 `ctx.parent` 会抛错；locale 服务上并没有 `t`，正确用法是 `ctx.locale.bind(ns)`）。**Host 半的改动必须换进程才能验证。**

#### 引导期的安全顺序（重要）

profile patch 在**你自己的用户目录**里（`$env:USERPROFILE\.dsh\profiles\desktop\cordis.patch.yml`），不可能随包交付，所以演练守卫需要你手动加一次。第一次安装时，正在运行的 Host 可能早于你最后一份代码；为避免误点造成「应用被关掉却没有重新拉起」，请**先加守卫再重启**：

```yaml
# $env:USERPROFILE\.dsh\profiles\desktop\cordis.patch.yml
- id: dsh-plugin-restart
  disabled: false
  config:
    dryRun: true
```

顺序：

1. 写入 `dryRun: true`，**先重启应用**（配置层是热生效的，守卫在旧代码上同样有效：按钮只会返回计划）。
2. 重启后跑下面的自检，确认 `supervisorScript` 指向本包的 `lib/restart-supervisor.ps1`，且 `supervisorRuntime.source` 是 `windows-powershell`（或你显式设置的 `DSH_POWERSHELL`）。
3. 把 `config: dryRun: true` 整段删掉（或改为 `false`），配置层热生效，**不需要再重启**——此后按钮执行真实一键重启。

### 引导后自检（非破坏性）

```powershell
# 计划与运行时证据（不产生任何副作用）
Invoke-RestMethod -Method Post -Uri http://127.0.0.1:19387/api/dsh-restart/status `
  -ContentType application/json -Body '{}' -Headers @{ Origin = 'http://127.0.0.1:19387' } |
  Select-Object -ExpandProperty value |
  Select-Object supervisorScript, supervisorSource, supervisorCandidates, supervisorRuntime, target

# 演练：只返回计划，绝不重启
Invoke-RestMethod -Method Post -Uri http://127.0.0.1:19387/api/dsh-restart/restart `
  -ContentType application/json -Body '{"dryRun":true}' -Headers @{ Origin = 'http://127.0.0.1:19387' }
```

`supervisorScript` 必须存在且指向本包的 `lib/restart-supervisor.ps1`；`supervisorRuntime.source` 为 `windows-powershell` 表示守护脚本用系统 PowerShell 5.1 启动，设为 `DSH_POWERSHELL` 时表示用了你指定的解释器。

卸载：`& $dsh plugin --profile desktop remove dsh-plugin-restart`。

## 使用

1. 重建你的插件（`pnpm build` 等），或从「设置 → 插件」安装/更新一个插件包。
2. 下一轮回复结束时，回复末尾会出现提示卡：**插件已更新，重启后生效** → `立即重启`（或 `稍后`）。
   - 也可以在配置的位置点图标按钮 → 确认面板 → `立即重启`。

# 自动开发调度器（dsh-orchestrator 系列）

plugins.description: DSH (DeepSeek Harness) browser plugin: your agent drives the Chrome you already use. Native messaging + real CDP, no port, no Connect button, 11 browser_* tools, on the Chrome Web Store. · 让 DSH 在你正在用的 Chrome 里动手。
plugins.readme_text:
English · 简体中文 · Development notes

--- **Give your DSH agent hands inside the Chrome you are already using** — your logins, your tabs, your session. Install once, no Connect button, ever. ![the in-page cursor driving a real page](assets/cursor-demo.gif) Every click flies a cursor to the target and labels what it is doing. It renders *inside the page*, so it lands in screenshots too — you and the model look at the same picture. ## ✨ Why another browser bridge? Every existing option makes you click something, every time: | Option | What goes wrong | |---|---| | `chrome-devtools-mcp --autoConnect` | Chrome asks *"Allow remote debugging?"* on **every** connection | | Browser MCP (store extension) | You must click the extension icon → **Connect** on **every** tab | | WebSocket-based bridges | Open a TCP port and trust anything that can reach it | | **dsh-chrome-bridge** | Nothing to click. Nothing listening on a port. | Three things make the difference: - 🔌 **Native messaging, not a port.** The extension talks to a local Node host over Chrome's native messaging pipe; the CLI reaches the host through a `0600` Unix socket guarded by a token. No TCP port to scan, no origin to spoof. - 🎯 **`chrome.debugger`, not injected scripts.** Clicks and keystrokes are dispatched as real CDP `Input.*` events, so they carry a user gesture — popups open, focus works, and sites that reject synthetic events behave normally. Screenshots, network, console and raw CDP come for free. - 👀 **A cursor the human can see.** A translucent light-blue arrow with a "🌐 DSH" name tag glides along a gentle arc to the target; the tag says what it is doing (click / type / drag / scroll) and each click leaves a soft ripple. It shares one style with the desktop cursor of [dsh-mac-computer-use](https://github.com/OrderG-X/dsh-mac-computer-use) (solid there, with a monitor icon), so you can tell at a glance whether the work is in the browser or on the desktop. It sits above modals and fullscreen, and picks up where it was after a navigation. Because it is rendered inside the page, **it appears in screenshots**. ## 🏗 Architecture ``` DSH's agent (provided by the harness — this repo ships none) ├── browser_* tools (DSH plugin) ─┐ └── cb CLI (shell) ─┤ ▼ Unix socket /tmp/dsh-bridge-/ (0700 dir + token) ▼ Node native host ←─ native messaging (stdio) ─→ Chrome extension (MV3) │ chrome.debugger ▼ real CDP ``` **This repo ships no agent** — the agent above is DSH's own; we only give it hands. The extension ID is fixed by the public key embedded in `plugin/vendor/extension/manifest.json`, so it is **identical on every machine** and the native-host registration never needs editing. The Web Store build has its own store-assigned ID; the host accepts both. ## 🚀 Install **The host ships inside the plugin package.** Adding the plugin copies the native host and the MV3 extension into place and registers native messaging for you — no `git clone`, no `install.sh`, no `python3`. Requirements: **macOS**, **Google Chrome 116+**, **Node.js 18+**. **1.** Sidebar → **Plugins** → **Add plugin** → paste this → Install → Enable → **restart DSH**: ``` https://github.com/OrderG-X/dsh-chrome-bridge/releases/latest/download/dsh-chrome-bridge.tgz ``` **2.** The plugin installs the host on first load (`~/.dsh/chrome-bridge`, `~/dsh-bridge-extension`, plus `com.dsh.bridge.json` in Chrome's `NativeMessagingHosts`). All that's left is getting the extension into Chrome — pick one: **Recommended: install from the Chrome Web Store** — open the [DSH Bridge store page](https://chromewebstore.google.com/detail/bippcbbbipppmhjkjomgdnjbooecbimo) → **Add to Chrome**. No Developer mode, and the extension updates itself. **Or: load it unpacked** (to run the newest extension from the repo). Chrome 137+ removed `--load-extension`, so that click has to be yours; the plugin walks you to it: - the first time a `browser_*` tool finds nothing to talk to, it **opens `chrome://extensions` in a background tab** and **puts `~/dsh-bridge-extension` on your clipboard** (once per session; the error text repeats the steps); - in the file picker press **⌘⇧G**, then **⌘V**, then Enter — no folder hunting. Do it once, ever: 1. open `chrome://extensions` 2. enable **Developer mode** (top right) 3. **Load unpacked** → **⌘⇧G** → **⌘V** → Enter (the folder is already on your clipboard) From a source checkout, `./bridge setup` does exactly this in one command: installs the host, opens the page, copies the path, and waits until the extension connects — printing ✅ when it does. **3.** Verify (the `cb` CLI is installed along the way): ```bash cb status # host pid … | extension connected: ✅ cb tabs ``` Until step 2 is done the `browser_*` tools fail **loudly with exactly these steps** — never silently. ### 🧩 The eleven native tools | Tool | What it does | |---|---| | `browser_tabs` | list / find / open / close / activate tabs | | `browser_read` | **numbered list of clickable / fillable elements** (`snapshot`), visible text, HTML, attributes, page info | | `browser_click` | click by element number (`ref`), selector, text, or coordinates | | `browser_input` | type, press keys, select, upload, hover, scroll | | `browser_nav` | go to a URL, **back / forward / reload**, and wait for load | | `browser_screenshot` | screenshot **returned as an image** (viewport / full / element) | | `browser_eval` | run JS in the page | | `browser_wait` | wait for an element, **a piece of text, or a URL** — or for it to go away (`gone`) | | `browser_dialog` | release alert / confirm / prompt | | `browser_drag` | drag by element number, selector, **visible text** or coordinates — HTML5 drag-and-drop and mouse-driven widgets (sliders, sortable lists) | | `browser_devtools` | **console output + uncaught JS errors, network requests (status, timing), a request's response body** | > A freshly installed bundle is not hot-loaded; DSH must be restarted once. > `dsh plugin add` from the CLI refuses the app-managed profile — use the sidebar there. > Plugin updates are not automatic in DSH yet: to upgrade, uninstall and install again. ### 👀 What you see while it works - **Click the toolbar icon** for a live panel: whether Chrome ↔ local host ↔ DSH are connected, **which DSH sessions are driving which tabs** (jump to a tab, or release it with one click), the last actions with their errors, a **pause switch** that makes the browser off-limits until you turn it back on, and *copy diagnostics* for bug reports. plugins.description: Plan Spend：DSH Web GUI 弹窗插件，展示已配置服务商的套餐花销（DeepSeek 官方余额 / OpenCode Go 5h·7d·月配额）
plugins.readme_text:
# @chi-hong22/dsh-plan-spend

A usage popup for the DSH Web GUI: the "Usage" sidebar navigation row opens a
panel showing the plan spend of the **configured** providers.

## What it shows

| Provider | Source | Rendered |
|---|---|---|
| DeepSeek official | the DeepSeek **account sign-in**: the host half asks `ctx.deepseekAccount.resolveToken` for the grant and calls `GET https://api.deepseek.com/user/balance` with `x-dsh-auth-token`; falls back to the same endpoint with `DEEPSEEK_API_KEY` | recharge balance (server precision kept), the topped-up split on the fallback card, the bonus wallet when the account holds one, the sufficiency flag, which route the number came from, and the **peak / off-peak** window with its next switch |
| OpenCode Go | `GET https://opencode.ai/zen/go/v1/usage` | 5-hour / 7-day / monthly used percentage, progress bar, reset countdown |

**赠金 (granted credit) gets its own row.** It is promotional and short-lived,
so it is not plan balance and does not count towards the recharge balance: when
the account actually holds some, the card adds a 赠金 line under the recharge
balance and hides it again at zero. Both routes map `granted_balance`; the
account card's headline figure still comes from `topped_up_balance` alone.

**Known limitation**: the OpenCode Go usage endpoint returns percentages and
reset instants only — no used/limit amounts. That column is therefore
percent-only; the exact dollar figures live in the OpenCode console.

## Peak and off-peak (DeepSeek official)

DeepSeek bills two rates, and off-peak is half the peak price, so the DeepSeek
card carries one more row: whether the current moment is peak or off-peak, and
how long until the next switch.

There is **no endpoint** that reports the current window — the rule lives in a
footnote on the pricing page — so this row derives it client-side from the
published rule:

- **Peak**: Monday–Friday `09:00–12:00` and `14:00–18:00` Beijing time (UTC
  `01:00–04:00` and `06:00–10:00`), **excluding Chinese public holidays**.
- **Everything else is off-peak**: `12:00–14:00`, the night, **all weekend**, and
  **public holidays in full**.

How the derivation is pinned down:

- **Weekends are always off-peak**, so a make-up workday that lands on a Saturday
  or Sunday needs no extra modelling — the weekend rule already calls it off-peak.
- The holiday set is therefore the **whole published State Council arrangement**
  (including workdays folded into a holiday, such as 2 January for New Year), not
  just the 11 statutory days; otherwise peak would reappear mid-holiday.
- Lookups use **UTC date keys**: every peak window lies inside UTC `00:00–16:00`
  and everything outside a window is off-peak, so a UTC-date lookup and a
  Beijing-date lookup agree.
- The windows are **half-open**: `04:00:00` sharp is already off-peak.

### The holiday table needs upkeep

The table is `UM_CHINA_PUBLIC_HOLIDAYS_UTC` in `client.body.js` (33 days for
2026, from State Council notice 国办发明电〔2025〕7 号); the years it covers are
listed in `UM_HOLIDAY_YEARS`. Each **fourth quarter**, once the State Council
publishes the next year's arrangement, append that year's date keys and the year
itself.

When the table does not cover the current year the card says so outright — the
holiday table does not cover that year, add the data — because in that state
every weekday statutory holiday would be scored as peak, and **a wrong number
stated silently is worse than a missing one declared**. A covered year shows no
notice at all.

## Install

```sh
dsh plugin --profile <profile> add github:Chi-hong22/dsh-plan-spend
```

> The `desktop` profile is owned by the Electron application: the CLI refuses it
> with `profile "desktop" is managed exclusively by the Electron application`.
> Install through the GUI plugin page instead.

Verify the mount:

```sh
dsh --profile <profile> --dump-config | grep dsh-plan-spend
```

## Configuration

The plugin has no config. It decides which providers to show from whether their
credential is configured; the reference names live in the `ADAPTERS` table in
`index.js`:

| Provider | Credential ref (POSIX environment name) |
|---|---|
| DeepSeek official | `DEEPSEEK_API_KEY` |
| OpenCode Go | `OPENCODEGO_API_KEY` |

Credentials resolve through `ctx.credentials.resolve()`; the source precedence
is documented by `@deepseek-ai/dsh-credentials-local` (launch environment →
stored file → project `.env` → harness home `.env`). **An unconfigured provider
issues no request** and renders as "no credential configured; skipped".

The API-key row is the **fallback**. The DeepSeek card is normally read in this
half from the signed-in DeepSeek account: `ctx.deepseekAccount.resolveToken`
hands out the stored grant for the configured inference origin
(`https://api.deepseek.com`), and that token goes to the same `/user/balance`
endpoint as `x-dsh-auth-token`. No API key is needed, and the grant never
reaches the browser. When the account cannot answer (signed out, no account
provider in this composition, or the query failed) the API-key card stands in
and names its own route; a failed account query is reported on that fallback
card, so "signed out" and "the query broke" stay distinguishable.

The account service's own balance query is deliberately **not** used: it goes to
`platform.deepseek.com`, whose WAF answers non-browser clients with HTTP 429,
so it reports a failed balance instead of a number.

A failed or missing API-key read also reports the effective credential's
**source layer** and whether this surface could write it
(`ctx.credentials.describe`), because "I saved a key and it still unauthorised"
is almost always a read-only launch-environment value winning over the stored
one.

Adding a provider = one row in `ADAPTERS` plus one reader function.

## Placement and sizing

The plugin registers two seats:

- **`sidebar.panellist`** (id `dsh-plan-spend`, order 20): the row. That seat is
  the sidebar's own navigation list, so the shell draws the button, its glyph
  box, its label, its active state and its collapsed rail; the entry only renders
  the gauge glyph at the size the shell hands down — **16px** on the sidebar,
  **18px** on the collapsed rail (`{ size, active }`) — and adds no pixels of its
  own. Clicking the row would normally make the shell select `dsh-plan-spend` as
  a main panel and throw, because none is registered, so the glyph claims the
  click in the document's capture phase — ahead of any delegated handler, under
  whatever root the shell mounts its tree — and toggles the panel instead.
- **`shell.overlay`** (id `dsh-plan-spend`): the panel. The frame-wide layer sits
  outside every column, so the panel renders *beside* the sidebar instead of
  being clipped by the sidebar's `overflow: hidden`.

**Placement**: the panel measures the frame-level column that holds the row (by
climbing the DOM to the frame's direct child, never by hashed class name) and
anchors its left edge 10px past that column's right edge. Its top edge follows
the conversation body instead of the workspace: the first
`[data-conversation-content]` beside the sidebar is the scroll area that sits
directly below the conversation header and its dialog/trajectory tabs, so the
panel starts 10px below *that* top and never covers the header or the tabs. With
no conversation on screen it falls back to the column's own top. It re-measures
when it opens, when the overlay resizes, and whenever that body changes size: a
header that grows as the tabs appear pushes the panel down with the body instead
of leaving it over the header.

**Dismissal**: the row again, the panel's `×`, `Esc`, or a press anywhere
outside the panel all close it.

**Resizing**: the grip sits in the panel's **bottom-right** corner — the one
farthest from the top anchor — dragging right grows the width and dragging down
grows the height. The size is stored under `dsh-plan-spend.size` and is bounded by the
panel minimum and the overlay bounds.

**Keyboard**: opening moves focus into the panel, and `Esc` closes it and hands
focus back to the row. `Tab` reaches the grip; the arrow keys resize in 16px
steps, and holding `Shift` makes each step four times

plugins.description: DSH Web GUI plugin: one conversation, one link — mirrors the main-view session into the URL fragment (and opens the linked conversation on load). Browser half only, no dependencies, no telemetry.
plugins.readme_text:
# dsh-session-url

**一个对话，一个链接。** DSH Web GUI 的地址栏永远指向主视图那个对话：切对话时地址栏跟着变，把 `#/session/<id>` 链接粘进地址栏就能打开相应对话。只有浏览器半区，没有宿主行为；**侧栏每一行本身就是链接**：在行上右键就是浏览器原生的「复制链接 / 在新标签页中打开链接」，中键或 Cmd+点击直接开新标签，而左键单击仍然只是切到那个对话。零依赖、零构建、不发网络请求。

[中文](#中文) · [English](#english)

---

## 中文

## 功能

- **视图 → 链接**：主视图在哪个对话，fragment 就变成 `#/session/<id>`。用 `history.replaceState` 写，**不新增历史记录**（返回键仍然是"离开 GUI"，不会被自己的跳转吃掉）。
- **链接 → 视图**：打开或粘贴 `#/session/<id>` 会打开那个对话。解析宽容：`#/sessions/<id>`、缺前导斜杠、URL 编码、尾部斜杠都认。
- **列表 → 链接**：**侧栏每一行本身就是链接**——一个覆盖整行的透明真锚点（`<a href="#/session/<id>" target="_blank">`）：右键就是浏览器原生菜单（在新标签页打开链接 / 复制链接 / 链接另存为），中键或 Cmd/Ctrl+点击直接开新标签；**左键单击仍然只是切到那个对话**（不新增历史记录）。行内官方控件被抬到锚点之上，不受影响。
- 只改 fragment：路径与查询串原样保留，启动 `?token=` 不会被破坏。

## 为什么用 fragment，而非路径或查询串

- 宿主的静态回退只对**解析到 dist 根**的路径返回 `index.html`，`/s/<id>` 会 404 —— 路径式深链起不来。
- 带启动 `?token=` 的请求会被 303 到干净的 `./`，多余查询串一律丢弃。fragment 不发给宿主，所以应用内跳转不会毁掉链接。

## 安装

```sh
dsh plugin --profile web add link:$PWD
# 或发布后：dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-session-url
```

浏览器半区在下一次页面刷新生效；行本身在宿主启动时生效（profile 设了 `patchReload: live` 时热加载）。

## 已知限制

- **8 秒权威窗口**：页面加载后 8 秒内，链接优先于"本地保存的选择"的恢复；这期间用户点击可能被链接抢回一次。窗口内目录还没列出的对话会被保留等待（没列出不等于死），窗口到期才丢弃并打一条 `[session-url]` 诊断。
- 已归档对话的链接**立即**拒绝，并打一条诊断。
- 只支持 fragment；带登录凭据的入口链接不可分享（token 在查询串里，不会写进链接）。
- 服务形态变化（`sessions` / `workspaces` / `uiWorkspace` 任一面不匹配）时插件自我禁用、只打一条诊断，不触碰官方行为。

- 整行链接依赖官方侧栏的行结构（`div[data-row-key="session:<id>"]`）：官方改了行标签或这个属性，链接会**静默消失**（地址栏同步不受影响）；不匹配的行一律不碰。

## 安全与隐私

浏览器半区只读目录快照、只调用官方 `openSession`；**不发网络请求、不打点、不写盘**（本仓没有家族单仓版本里的每日心跳遥测）。

## English

## Features

- **View to link**: the conversation the main view is in becomes the fragment `#/session/<id>`. It is written with `history.replaceState`, so **no history entry is added** (Back still leaves the GUI; it is not eaten by our own jumps).
- **Link to view**: opening or pasting `#/session/<id>` opens that conversation. Parsing is tolerant: `#/sessions/<id>`, a missing leading slash, URL encoding and a trailing slash are all accepted.
- **List to link**: **every sidebar row is itself the link** — a transparent real anchor covering the row (`<a href="#/session/<id>" target="_blank">`): right click gives the browser's native menu (open link in new tab / copy link / save link as), middle or Cmd/Ctrl click opens a new tab, while a plain left click still only switches to that conversation (no history entry). The row's own controls are lifted above the anchor, so they keep working.
- Only the fragment changes: path and query are preserved as they are, so a launch `?token=` is not damaged.

## Why the fragment, and not a path or query

- The host's static fallback serves `index.html` only for a path that resolves to the dist root; `/s/<id>` is a 404 — a path-style deep link cannot boot the GUI.
- A request that still carries the launch `?token=` is answered with a 303 to the clean `./`, and every extra query parameter is dropped. The fragment is not sent to the host, so in-app navigation cannot destroy the link.

## Install

```sh
dsh plugin --profile web add link:$PWD
# or, once published: dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-session-url
```

The browser half takes effect on the next page load; the row itself loads at host start (or hot-loads when the profile sets `patchReload: live`).

## Known limitations

- **Eight-second authority window**: for 8 s after a page load a link outranks the restore of the locally saved selection, so a click during boot can be overridden once. A linked conversation the catalog has not listed yet is kept waiting (unlisted is not death) and dropped only at expiry, with one `[session-url]` diagnostic.
- A link to an archived conversation is refused **immediately**, with one diagnostic.
- Fragment only; an entry link carrying credentials is not shareable (the token lives in the query and is never written into the link).
- If the service shape changes (any of `sessions` / `workspaces` / `uiWorkspace` no longer matches), the plugin disables itself with a single diagnostic and leaves the official behavior untouched.

- The row-wide link depends on the official sidebar row markup (`div[data-row-key="session:<id>"]`): if the row tag or that attribute changes, the link silently disappears (the address-bar sync is unaffected), and unmatched rows are never touched.

## Security and privacy

The browser half only reads catalog snapshots and calls the official `openSession`. It sends **no network request, no telemetry, and writes nothing to disk** (the family monorepo build's daily heartbeat is not part of this repository).

## 开发日志 / Dev log

跨机改动记录在私有库 [DDDMUC/repo-devlogs](https://github.com/DDDMUC/repo-devlogs) 的 `dsh-session-url/` 文件夹；见本仓 `AGENTS.md`。

## License

MIT
