# DSH MCP Server

[![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-MIT-yellow.svg)](LICENSE)

A DeepSeek Harness (DSH) plugin that publishes a **Model Context Protocol (MCP)** server from the
running Harness host, so other agent harnesses — Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, another DSH, any MCP
client — can call DSH: start sessions, drive turns, wait for them, read transcripts, and cancel work.

The plugin is a Host-only bundle with **zero dependencies** (no DSH import, no third-party module),
so it installs into a profile and survives Harness upgrades that keep the service contracts.
Every request is attributed to the calling agent and every session is recorded against its creator,
so several harnesses can share one endpoint and still ask "which sessions are mine?".

The same tool table is also registered into the local Harness, so a DSH agent calls these tools
directly — switchable on this bundle's row in the Web **Plugins** page, and clamped to the calling
session's own authority (see [DSH-local tools](#dsh-local-tools)).

```
other harness ──MCP (Streamable HTTP or stdio)──> DSH MCP Server ──> DSH services
                                                                     sessionController / sessionQuery / tools
```

## Architecture

The plugin is an adapter between two contracts: MCP on the outside, DSH services on the inside. Nothing it
ships imports a DSH package, so every layer talks through `ctx` and plain data.

| Module | Role |
|---|---|
| [`index.js`](index.js) | Composition root: reads the row config, registers the routes and the local tools, and owns the plugin's `ctx.effect`s (endpoint publication, route/tool/state disposal) so a reload unwinds what it created. |
| [`lib/protocol.js`](lib/protocol.js) | MCP wire: JSON-RPC envelope, protocol-version negotiation, error codes, gateway dispatch. |
| [`lib/http-route.js`](lib/http-route.js) / [`bin/dsh-mcp-stdio.mjs`](bin/dsh-mcp-stdio.mjs) | The two transports: Streamable HTTP on the Harness listener, and a stdio bridge that forwards to that same endpoint. |
| [`lib/dsh-capabilities.js`](lib/dsh-capabilities.js) | The DSH-facing tools and resources; each maps onto live services (`sessionController`, `sessionQuery`, `tools`, …). |
| [`lib/authority.js`](lib/authority.js) | The authority arithmetic those tools are clamped by: the sandbox ladder, workspace containment, and the `cwd` clamp. |
| [`lib/dsh-contracts.js`](lib/dsh-contracts.js) | The shape of the events and messages the tools read: session ids, message prose, transcript rows, turn numbers, failure text — one definition instead of a copy per caller. Transport-level error formatting stays with the transport. |
| [`lib/dsh-tools-bridge.js`](lib/dsh-tools-bridge.js) | The same table exposed *into* DSH: the three-tool front door or the full registry installed in the injected tools scope, plus tools opened lazily in the calling agent's own scope. |
| [`lib/clients.js`](lib/clients.js) | Caller identity and session ownership: header/`clientInfo`/User-Agent, a 0600 registry, and the owner a session is recorded against. |
| [`lib/config-route.js`](lib/config-route.js) + [`lib/client.js`](lib/client.js) | Control plane: a loopback JSON route and the browser panel that reads and writes it — registered both as a first-level Settings section and as the bundle row's Configure page. |
| [`lib/transcript.js`](lib/transcript.js) | Windowed transcript reads: tail/head/outline, role and sequence filters, per-message caps and the response budget. |
| [`work-sync.js`](work-sync.js) | The **second bundle row**: mounts task-start progress sync, publishes it as the `workSync` service, and owns its own config. |
| [`lib/work-sync.js`](lib/work-sync.js) | The sync engine itself: who to ask, claim correlation, deadlines — built only on `session/event`. |
| [`lib/workspace-grouping.js`](lib/workspace-grouping.js) | Put a session this endpoint starts into the sidebar project its directory already has. |

Three rules keep the layering honest. **Services, not re-implementations**: transcript reads replay the durable
event log, permissions come from `permissionPresets`, sidebar membership from `workspaceRegistry`. **Narrow
seams**: the transport never touches a session, and the capabilities never touch a socket. **Only own state on
disk**: everything this plugin persists is its own state (`$DSH_HOME/mcp/*.json` by default; `endpointFile` and
`clientsFile` move it) at mode 0600 — never a session, a transcript, or a setting DSH already owns.

## What it exposes

| MCP tool | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `dsh_run_prompt` | Start a **new** DSH session and run one prompt; returns the assistant's final text and the new `sessionId`. Supports `cwd`, `agentPreset`, `permissionPreset`, `model` (`provider/model`), `wait: false`, `timeoutMs`. |
| `dsh_continue_session` | Send a prompt to an **existing** session (resuming it if it is cold). Keeps the session's context and workspace; `permissionPreset` re-pins the session's sandbox mode and approval policy before the prompt, and `model` (`provider/model`) overrides the session's model. Without `model` the session keeps the model it already runs. |
| `dsh_list_commands` | The slash commands a session's agent can currently run: the global command layer plus whatever that agent's preset composes, so availability differs per agent preset. |
| `dsh_run_command` | Run one slash command in a session and return its settled `{ kind, text, commandId }`. `line` takes a complete command line (`"/compact"`, `"/permission danger-full-access"`); `command` (+ optional `args`) takes a bare name. The command executes immediately without a model turn. |
| `dsh_list_sessions` | A page of the session index: `sessionId`, title, running state, archival state, activity time, and the recorded owning agent (`view: "full"` adds cwd and liveness). Narrow server-side with `query` (title/cwd/owner/id), `mine: true` (or the `restrictToOwner` setting), `owner: "<id>"` (narrowing only: on a restricted endpoint another owner is refused), and `running`; page with `cursor`/`nextCursor`. Archived sessions are hidden unless `includeArchived: true`, mirroring the Web UI. |
| `dsh_read_session` | A window of one session's transcript (user-authored and assistant messages only), plus the last durable `permissionPreset`. `mode: "tail"` (default, last 10) / `"head"` / `"outline"` (one compact row per message with a preview and length, no full text); `roles`, `afterSeq` + `window.nextAfterSeq` to page, `maxChars` (default 2000) to cap a single answer. Reports `totalMessages`, `matchedMessages` and `returned`, so the caller always knows what it has not read. `limit: 0` asks for the largest window (capped at 1000 messages), and one response is capped at about 512K characters (`truncatedByBudget`), so a read can never dump a whole long session. Works while the session is archived. |
| `dsh_answer_request` | Answer a parked decision, only when the deployment sets `answerUserRequests: true`: `decision: "allow"|"deny"` for an approval (a one-shot grant, or a denial) or `answers: [{ id, selected }]` for a question. Ids come from `dsh_list_requests`, which marks what this endpoint parked with `answerable: true`. The GUI stays in the race — whoever decides first wins — and an unanswered request still fails closed at `requestAnswerTimeoutMs`. An internal DSH caller may only settle an **approval** while it already holds `danger-full-access`; questions are always answerable (see [DSH-local tools](#dsh-local-tools)). |
| `dsh_wait_session` | Block until the turn a session is already running ends, then return the assistant text it produced — for `wait: false` starts, GUI-driven sessions, or another caller's work. Never prompts, steers, or cancels: reaching `timeoutMs` returns `status: "timedOut"` with the turn still running, so call it again; `status: "idle"` returns immediately when nothing is running. |
| `dsh_list_requests` | The user decisions a session — or the newest visible sessions, running first — is waiting on: approval requests (`approval/asked` with no matching `approval/decided`, the one-shot permission decision behind a sandbox escalation) and unanswered `ask_u

# DSH 提示词增强器

**简体中文** ｜ [English](README.en.md)

DeepSeek Harness（DSH）插件。在输入框写提示词，点一下按钮，模型改写后替换输入框内容。

- 包名：`@jianyiagi/dsh-prompt-enhancer`
- 仓库：https://github.com/JianYiAG/dsh-prompt-enhancer
- 许可：MIT

---

## 安装

**桌面端**：

1. 左侧栏进「插件」页
2. 安装 bundle，填 `@jianyiagi/dsh-prompt-enhancer`
3. 完全退出应用后重新打开

**CLI / Web 端**：

```powershell
dsh plugin --profile <profile> add @jianyiagi/dsh-prompt-enhancer
```

CLI 安装后若未生效，在「插件」页勾选该插件，或把包名加入 profile `package.json` 的 `dsh.profile.bundles`，然后重启应用。

安装与常见问题见 [DISTRIBUTION.md](DISTRIBUTION.md)。

---

## 使用

1. 在输入框输入提示词
2. 点模型选择器左侧的按钮
3. 按钮停止转动后，输入框内容已替换为改写结果；不满意可在输入框内撤销

输入框为空时按钮不显示。

也可输入 `/prompt-enhance 提示词`，结果以命令结果行显示，不写回输入框。

---

## 配置

默认使用当前会话的模型。可在 profile 补丁中指定固定模型：

```yaml
- insert:
    - id: prompt-enhancer
      name: '@jianyiagi/dsh-prompt-enhancer'
      config:
        provider: <provider-id>
        model: <model-id>
```

两个字段需同时提供；删除 `config` 即恢复使用会话模型。

---

## 卸载

桌面端在「插件」页卸载；CLI：

```powershell
dsh plugin --profile <profile> remove @jianyiagi/dsh-prompt-enhancer
```

---

MIT

plugins.readme_text:
# dsh-mcp-master

English | [中文](README.zh.md)

**MCP Master for [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness).** Choose which MCP servers each session uses — from your **global** list and the workspace's **project** list — with a picker that sits right before the composer's model selector. Pick them when a session starts, and switch them at any time afterwards, just like the model.

- **Project servers** come from the files other agents already use: `.mcp.json` (Claude Code), `.cursor/mcp.json`, `.vscode/mcp.json`, `.dsh/mcp.json`.
- **Global servers** come from `~/.dsh/mcp-master/mcp.json` (same `mcpServers` format). A project server shadows a global one of the same name.

```json
// <workspace>/.mcp.json  or  ~/.dsh/mcp-master/mcp.json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "orion-mcp":            { "command": "uv", "args": ["run", "--project", ".", "orion-mcp"] },
    "atlassian-mcp-server": { "type": "http", "url": "https://mcp.atlassian.com/v1/mcp/authv2" },
    "conduktor-console":    { "command": "npx", "args": ["mcp-remote", "https://…/api/mcp", "--header", "Authorization: Bearer ${CONDUKTOR_API_TOKEN}"], "enabled": false }
  }
}
```

## The picker

`[ 🔌 MCP 2 ● ]  [ model ▾ ]  [ ➤ ]` — in the composer row of every session, including a brand-new one.

- **Zero footprint when unused**: no global or project servers → nothing renders.
- **Chip**: number of servers active in this session and one status dot for them (green connected · amber sign-in needed · red failing · pulsing starting). A small blue dot means project servers await review.
- **Panel** (click the chip; Esc / click outside to close): *Project* and *Global* groups. Each row has a **checkbox = use in this session**, status, transport, a `default` tag, and inline **Sign in** / **Retry**. Expand a row for the command/URL (as written — never variable-expanded), auth, server version, tools, logs, Reconnect, Sign out, Revoke trust.
- **Footer**: what new sessions start with, and **Use for new sessions** to save the current selection as this workspace's default (**Reset** returns to the files' own `enabled` flags).
- Theme tokens only (light/dark follow the app); copy follows **Settings → General → Language**.

## How sessions get servers

| Topic | Behavior |
|---|---|
| New session | Starts from the workspace default: the saved one, or else every trusted server whose file entry is not `"enabled": false` / `"disabled": true`. |
| Forks & subagents | Inherit the parent session's selection (`parentSession`). |
| Switching later | Checking/unchecking registers/unregisters that server's tools in **this session only**, from the next step on. DSH itself records tool additions/removals in the session log (`developer/message` tool-addition/removal), so history, resume, and replay stay consistent — unlike an agent preset, which is a whole plugin composition and therefore locked once the session starts. |
| Persistence | Selections, defaults, trust, and OAuth tokens live in `~/.dsh/mcp-master/state.json` (0600). Config files are never modified. |
| Process lifetime | A server runs while a live session — or a session open in the UI but not started yet — selects it; it stops 2 minutes after the last one deselects it, and a workspace with no sessions or viewers shuts down after 15 idle minutes. |

## Trust (project servers)

A `.mcp.json` in a cloned repository can run any command, so project servers must be **trusted** before they run (same model as Claude Code's project-server approval). Checking an untrusted server shows the exact command/URL with **Trust & use**. Trust is per workspace and bound to the entry as written: if the command, args, env, URL, or headers change, the server becomes **Changed** and needs review again. Global servers are yours and always trusted. `autoTrust: true` skips the review.

## Transports and auth

- **stdio** (own process group, reaped with its children; cwd = workspace root), **Streamable HTTP** (session ids, SSE responses, `list_changed` stream), **legacy HTTP+SSE** (automatic fallback). Server→client `ping` / `roots/list` are answered.
- **OAuth** per the MCP authorization spec: RFC 9728 → RFC 8414/OIDC discovery → RFC 7591 dynamic client registration → authorization code + PKCE (S256) with RFC 8707 `resource`, then refresh. Tokens are keyed by server URL, so one sign-in covers every workspace. An explicit `Authorization` header is used as-is; `"oauth": { "clientId", "clientSecret", "scope" }` covers providers without dynamic registration.
- **Variables**: `${VAR}`, `${VAR:-default}`, `${env:VAR}`, `${workspaceFolder}` — resolved from DSH's environment layered over your login-shell environment (so `~/.zshrc` exports and your shell `PATH` work in the desktop app).
- **Tools** are named `mcp__<server>__<tool>` like the built-in MCP client; input schemas are folded into the registry's JSON-Schema subset (`$ref`, nullable `anyOf`, type arrays, `allOf`; dropped constraints become description hints); `readOnlyHint` tools may run in parallel.

## Configuration (optional)

```yaml
# your profile's cordis.patch.yml
- id: mcp-master
  name: dsh-mcp-master
  config:
    globalConfigFile: ~/.dsh/mcp-master/mcp.json   # false disables the global scope
    configFiles: [.mcp.json, .cursor/mcp.json, .vscode/mcp.json, .dsh/mcp.json]
    autoTrust: false
    searchParents: true          # also look in parent directories of the session cwd
    startupWaitMs: 5000          # a new session waits this long for selected servers that are still starting
    connectTimeoutMs: 60000
    toolCallTimeoutMs: 300000
    idleShutdownMinutes: 15
```

## Security notes

- `/mcp-master/api/*` passes DSH's connection fence (Host/Origin + browser authentication); mutating calls also need a custom header that cross-origin pages cannot send without a CORS preflight; paths must be inside registered workspaces or live session directories.
- The OAuth redirect (`/mcp-master/oauth/callback`) opens in your system browser without the DSH cookie and is authorized by a single-use 192-bit `state`.
- Logs and the UI redact codes, tokens, and `Bearer` values; command lines are shown unexpanded. `state.json` holds tokens — treat it like a credentials file.

## Develop

```sh
pnpm install
pnpm run verify          # build + typecheck + tests (node --test runs the .ts tests directly)
```

| Path | Role |
|---|---|
| `src/index.ts` | Host entry: options, agent lifecycle hooks, route mounting |
| `src/host/config.ts` | Catalog discovery (project + global), dialects, variable expansion, fingerprints |
| `src/host/runtime.ts` | Trust, defaults, per-session selections, server lifecycle, per-agent tool registration |
| `src/host/state.ts` | Persistent state (`~/.dsh/mcp-master/state.json`) |
| `src/host/stdio.ts`, `http.ts`, `jsonrpc.ts` | MCP transports and JSON-RPC plumbing (zero runtime dependencies) |
| `src/host/oauth.ts` | MCP authorization (discovery, DCR, PKCE, refresh) |
| `src/host/schema.ts`, `tools.ts` | Schema folding and ToolDefinitions |
| `src/host/api.ts` | HTTP API + OAuth callback |
| `src/client/*` | Composer picker (React; `__ModuleLoader__` bundle; portal popover like the model menu) |
| `src/shared/types.ts` | Wire contract between the halves |

After rebuilding an installed copy, restart DSH: the Host module is an ES module and is not re-imported in place.

## License

MIT

plugins.description: Per-workspace persistent memory plugin for DeepSeek Harness (DSH): sidebar panel, automatic system-prompt injection, and an agent tool to save memories
plugins.readme_text:
# dsh-workspace-memories

English | [中文](README.zh.md)

[![](https://img.shields.io/badge/powered_by-dsh-4D6BFE?style=flat-square&logo=deepseek&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness)
[![](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/dsh-workspace-memories?style=flat-square)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/dsh-workspace-memories)
[![](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-blue?style=flat-square)](LICENSE)

**Per-workspace persistent memory for [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) (DSH)** — a plugin that gives every workspace its own durable memory files, injects them into every session running in that workspace, and lets both you and the agent manage them.

## Why this plugin exists

DSH agents are stateless across sessions: everything a session "learns" — your project's decisions, conventions, hard-won debugging facts — lives only in that conversation's context and is gone when it ends. The built-in mechanism for durable knowledge is `AGENTS.md`, but it is a static, project-owned instruction file: the agent cannot update it on its own, and **some things should not live in the project folder at all** — server addresses and topologies, local environment quirks, machine-specific paths, personal working conventions. Anything under the project tree risks being committed to git by accident.

This plugin closes that gap with a small, explicit memory loop whose default storage is **outside the project directory**:

1. **Every workspace gets a memory directory** — by default under the DSH data directory (`~/.dsh/workspace-memory/<workspace>/`), never inside the repo. Plain Markdown you can read, diff, and back up. (An opt-in `workspace` storage mode keeps memories in `<workspace>/.dsh/memory/` for teams who *want* them versioned alongside the code.)
2. **Memories are injected automatically** — each session created in a workspace carries that workspace's memory files in its system prompt, alongside `AGENTS.md`, so a fresh session starts already "remembering".
3. **The agent can write memories itself** — a global `save_workspace_memory` tool lets any session persist a decision, server detail, convention, or preference the moment you say "remember this".
4. **You stay in control** — a sidebar panel lists, creates, edits, and deletes memory files per workspace, so memory stays inspectable and correctable instead of hidden in a database.

## Features

| Capability | Where |
|---|---|
| Browse / create / edit / delete memory files | **Workspace Memory** sidebar panel (switch workspaces via the selector) |
| Ask the agent to remember something | Any session: "remember: …" → the agent calls `save_workspace_memory` |
| Automatic recall | Every session in the workspace gets its memory files injected into its system prompt |

Works in every built-in agent preset (Standard, PTC, Minimal, Creator): the tool is registered in the root composition, and global tools are visible to all presets unless a custom preset opts out with a `tools.restrict` allow list — add `save_workspace_memory` to that list if so.

## Installation

The package is plain JavaScript with no build step, so every install channel works:

```sh
# from npm (once published)
dsh plugin --profile desktop add dsh-workspace-memories

# straight from GitHub (no build script needed — sources ship as-is)
dsh plugin --profile desktop add github:lengfengng-tech/dsh-workspace-memories

# from a local checkout
dsh plugin --profile desktop add ./dsh-workspace-memories
```

Or use the GUI: sidebar **Plugins → Add plugin**, paste a package name, GitHub address, or absolute local path, then **Enable now**.

Uninstall: the Plugins page, or `dsh plugin --profile desktop remove dsh-workspace-memories`.

## Usage

- Open the **Workspace Memory** entry in the sidebar. The selector defaults to the workspace of the current session. **New file** creates a `.md` memory (the extension is added when missing); select a file to edit, save, or delete it.
- Tell the agent "remember: this project uses pnpm, not npm" — it writes a memory file that every session of the workspace (and the panel) sees immediately.
- Storage and layout are configurable: `storage: home` (default, DSH data directory, outside the project) or `storage: workspace` (inside the project at `directory`, default `.dsh/memory`).

## Important: start a new session after installing or upgrading

Tool registration takes effect immediately on the host, but **a model's visible tool list is assembled when each conversation turn starts**:

- If a session's current turn began *before* the plugin was installed or reloaded, that turn's tool declaration is stale. This is most visible in **PTC mode**, where the model reads a pre-generated TypeScript binding (`ToolArgsMap`) that does not yet contain `save_workspace_memory` — the model may conclude "there is no memory tool", or fall back to probing the tool by name through the code channel (which actually works, since dispatch goes through the live host registry).
- **The fix is simple: start a new session, or just send a new message after the current turn ends.** The next turn regenerates the tool declaration and `save_workspace_memory` appears normally — no probing needed.

Memory injection into the system prompt is attached when an agent is created (session start, resume after a restart, clear, or compaction); once attached, a session picks up changed memory files on its next step automatically.

## Data layout and safety

Two storage modes, chosen by the plugin's `storage` config:

| Mode | Memory location | Use it for |
|---|---|---|
| `home` (default) | `~/.dsh/workspace-memory/<workspace-key>/` — outside the project | Machine-local or sensitive notes: server configs, environment quirks, personal conventions |
| `workspace` | `<workspace>/.dsh/memory/` — inside the project | Team-shared memories meant to be committed alongside the code |

```
~/.dsh/workspace-memory/     # default memory store, one subdirectory per workspace
dsh-workspace-memories/        # this plugin
├── package.json             #   bundle manifest (dsh.bundle.patch + dsh.client)
├── cordis.patch.yml         #   plugin row declaration
├── index.js                 #   host: /api routes + prompt injection + the save tool
├── client.js                #   browser: sidebar entry + management panel
├── locale/                  #   panel copy (en, zh)
├── icon.svg
└── selftest.mjs             #   host-logic self-test: node selftest.mjs
```

Safety constraints: the browser panel can only address registered workspaces by `workspaceId` (no arbitrary host paths); file names are strictly validated (no path separators, `..`, whitespace, or control characters); one file is capped at 1 MiB; prompt injection truncates each file to 32K characters and caps at 20 files.

## Development

- Install with a `link:` dependency (local-path install does this): editing `client.js` hot-reloads in the page via the client HMR receiver; editing `index.js` (host code) requires a DSH restart to load the new module generation.
- Run the self-test: `node selftest.mjs` (mocks the plugin context; covers routes, prompt rendering, tool writes, and validation failures).
- Runtime checks: host entry `include:workspace-memory` should be `active`; the client slot `sidebar.panellist` should list a `workspace-memory` occupant; `save_workspace_memory` should appear in the tool list.

## License

[MIT](LICENSE) — © 2026 lengfengng-tech

---

This is a community plugin built on [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness); it is not an official DeepSeek product. Naming follows the [DSH brand guidelines](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/main/BRAND_GUIDELINES.md).

plugins.readme_text:
# Opfield plugins for DeepSeek Harness

[![M8ven Score](https://m8ven.ai/badge/mcp/opfield/dsh-plugins)](https://m8ven.ai/mcp/opfield/dsh-plugins?s=readme)

Plugins for [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) (DSH).

| Package | What it does |
|---|---|
| [`@opfield/dsh-mcp-hub`](packages/mcp-hub) | Every MCP server in one place: eager / lazy / auto tool exposure per server, OAuth for HTTP servers, direct launch of `npx` packages, and an API for plugins that bring their own servers. Works with any MCP server, not only Opfield. |
| [`@opfield/dsh-opfield`](packages/opfield) | Opfield instances as MCP servers, models from one instance with an automatic inference token and model sync, plus budget, prompt-cache timer and `/compact` offer components. Requires MCP Hub. |
| [`@opfield/dsh-multi-repo`](packages/multi-repo) | Multi-root workspaces: attach other repositories to a workspace. Attached roots are writable under `workspace-write`, listed in the model context with their `AGENTS.md`, and edited from the composer or `/roots`. Works on its own. |

## Install

In DSH open **Plugins → Add plugin**, enter a spec from the table, then **Enable now**. Install MCP Hub first: the Opfield plugin needs it. Restart DSH after adding Opfield.

| Plugin | From npm | From this repository |
|---|---|---|
| MCP Hub | `@opfield/dsh-mcp-hub` | `github:opfield/dsh-plugins#path:/packages/mcp-hub` |
| Opfield | `@opfield/dsh-opfield` | `github:opfield/dsh-plugins#path:/packages/opfield` |
| Multi-root workspaces | `@opfield/dsh-multi-repo` | `github:opfield/dsh-plugins#path:/packages/multi-repo` |

To pin a version from the repository, add its tag before `path`: `github:opfield/dsh-plugins#mcp-hub-v0.4.1&path:/packages/mcp-hub`, `github:opfield/dsh-plugins#opfield-v0.5.2&path:/packages/opfield`.

Then open **Plugins → Opfield → Add instance**, enter the instance address and press **Sign in**. Each package's README covers the details: [MCP Hub](packages/mcp-hub#install), [Opfield](packages/opfield#install), [Multi-root workspaces](packages/multi-repo#install).

DSH does not update plugins yet: to upgrade, remove the plugin and add the new version.

## Development

```sh
npm install   # Harness packages the tests run against
npm test
```

The plugins have no build step. To try a working copy, add it in DSH by absolute path (`/path/to/dsh-plugins/packages/mcp-hub`).

## Release

Bump `version` in `packages/<dir>/package.json`, commit, and push a tag `<dir>-v<version>`, for example `mcp-hub-v0.4.1`. The Release workflow tests, publishes the package to npm with provenance, and creates a GitHub release.

## License

[MIT](LICENSE)

plugins.description: DeepSeek Harness plugin: identify the provider behind the current model route and query its API balance or subscription quota. No subprocesses, no exec permissions, official endpoints only.
plugins.readme_text:
[中文](README.zh-CN.md) | **English**

# Balance & Quota · dsh-balance-meter

> A small plugin for DeepSeek Harness: **it tells you how much credit or quota is left for the model you're actually using.**

No control panels to open, no mental arithmetic, and no being fooled by a stale number — if it genuinely can't read your balance, it says why.

![The balance readout under the composer](docs/images/chip.png)

Click it to open the full panel:

![The balance and quota panel](docs/images/panel.png)

---

## What problem it solves

Running an agent on API credit or a subscription, two things bite:

1. **You run out mid-task** and only find out when it breaks.
2. **You juggle several dashboards** — DeepSeek, Kimi, Zhipu — and they don't even report the same thing: some give money, some give percentages.

This plugin gathers it into one place: **whichever provider your current session is using, it reads that provider's balance** and shows it the same way every time.

---

## What it can read

Balances are **per provider**, not per model — every model under one provider shares the same pool.

### ✅ Supported: 9 built-in providers

| Provider | What it reads | Shown as |
|---|---|---|
| **DeepSeek** | account balance | money (`¥12.34`) |
| **OpenRouter** | key credit | money |
| **Moonshot / Kimi** | account balance | money |
| **SiliconFlow** | account balance | money |
| **智谱 GLM / Z.AI** | subscription quota | window percentages |
| **Kimi Coding** | subscription quota | window percentages |
| **MiniMax** | plan quota | window percentages |
| **OpenCode Go** | subscription quota | window percentages |
| **OpenDesign (AMR)** | wallet + Design Plan windows | money + percentages |

"Window percentages" means the plugin lists each quota period separately — rolling / weekly / monthly — with its own bar and reset time. So you can tell whether the 5-hour window is nearly spent or the monthly total is running out.

### ⚠️ May work: common relay panels

If you use a **self-hosted relay** (New-API, Sub2API, CloseAI, claude-code-hub and similar), the plugin tries a set of conventional endpoints in order:

```
/api/usage/token/  →  /v1/dashboard/billing/subscription  →  /v1/usage
→  /api/v1/me/quota  →  /dashboard/billing/credit_grants
→  /api/v1/credits  →  /api/user/self
```

Whichever returns a readable figure first wins. **An endpoint you configure yourself is tried before all of them.**

> The mechanism (ordering, short-circuiting, unit calibration) is covered by tests, but **each preset's response shape was transcribed from public panel documentation and the author cannot verify them all against live servers**. So an unrecognised shape is reported as "reachable but unparseable" with the raw response attached — never guessed at.

### ❌ Not supported

| Situation | What happens |
|---|---|
| **The vendor has no public balance endpoint** | Says so plainly; invents nothing |
| **Route isn't in the catalog and no preset matched** | Reports "not catalogued" plus the last raw response |
| **No credential configured** | Names the variable you need to set |
| **Endpoint answered but the shape is unknown** | Reports "unparseable" with an excerpt (secrets masked) |

"Not catalogued" means **this plugin doesn't recognise that provider yet** — it does not mean the vendor has no balance endpoint. Setting a custom endpoint via `balance_set_endpoint` usually fixes it.

---

## Install

```sh
dsh plugin --profile desktop add @zhujiuyi/dsh-balance
```

Then **restart DSH**. The readout appears on the stats row under the composer.

> Don't install `dsh-balance-meter` (no scope). That name belongs to an unrelated package on npm.

Prefer not to use npm? Install the tarball from a release instead — `/latest/` follows the newest one, so this command needs no editing:

```sh
dsh plugin --profile desktop add https://github.com/zhujiuyi/dsh-balance-meter/releases/latest/download/zhujiuyi-dsh-balance-0.2.5.tgz
```

Installing from the repository works too:

```sh
dsh plugin --profile desktop add github:zhujiuyi/dsh-balance-meter
```

Uninstall:

```sh
dsh plugin --profile desktop remove @zhujiuyi/dsh-balance
```

---

## Using it

Mostly you don't do anything. Three ways in:

1. **Glance** — the readout is always on the stats row: money for API credit, a percentage for subscriptions.
2. **Click** — provider, billing mode, endpoint, last-read time, and every quota window with its own bar.
3. **Ask** — say "how much quota is left" and the agent calls the `balance_check` tool.

---

## On getting the number right

This is what the plugin cares about most. Three rules:

**1. It never guesses.** If it can't read a figure it says so and explains why. "Unavailable" beats a plausible-looking wrong number.

**2. Stale figures are labelled.** If a refresh fails after a previous success, the readout keeps showing the last known value marked "possibly stale", with the failure reason in the details. An old number is never passed off as current.

**3. The trend chart uses real readings only.** That curve comes from reads that actually happened, not a hardcoded sample series. With fewer than two readings it says it's still collecting rather than drawing a fake history.

### When it refreshes automatically

- **After each finished turn** — refreshed once
- **A background check every 15 seconds** — refreshes if policy allows
- **A reading older than 5 minutes** — forced refresh (configurable)
- **You click "Refresh now"** — always

Two limits keep it polite: a **minimum interval** (30s by default) and a **failure cooldown**. Nothing polls while the page is hidden.

---

## OpenDesign users: one extra step

OpenDesign is the only provider whose **billing is not on the API gateway host**, and it needs a login first:

```sh
vela login          # or sign in through the OpenDesign desktop app
```

That writes a credential to `~/.amr/config.json`, which the plugin reads.

**Why this is required:** the `sk-amr-…` API key you configure in DSH is a *runtime* key for inference, and the vendor explicitly rejects it for billing reads. Balance can only be read with the control key that signing in produces.

Signed out, the plugin tells you to run `vela login` — it never treats that gateway as an uncatalogued relay and starts probing it.

---

## Configuration

Plugins page → the `@zhujiuyi/dsh-balance` card: preferred route, auto-refresh on/off, minimum interval, and the refresh-after ceiling.

To pin a custom endpoint or credential variable for one route, edit the `balance-meter` row in your profile's `cordis.patch.yml`:

```yaml
- id: balance-meter
  name: "@zhujiuyi/dsh-balance"
  config:
    primary: deepseek
    routes:
      - id: my-provider
        baseURL: https://api.example.com/v1
        apiKeyEnv: MY_PROVIDER_API_KEY
        endpoint: '{origin}/v1/balance'
```

Templates support `{origin}` (scheme + host) and `{base}` (the full baseURL). Prefer `{origin}` — it doesn't care whether your baseURL carries a path segment.

---

## Privacy

- **No `exec` permission, no subprocesses** — no shell, no curl.
- **Requests go only to the gateway you configured** — no third-party domains, no telemetry, no phone-home.
- **Keys are used for that gateway only** — read from DSH's credential store, put in a request header, never written to disk, logs, or the browser snapshot. The snapshot carries variable *names* only (there's a test asserting this).
- **Nothing else in DSH is modified** — only this plugin's own config row.

---

## For developers

```sh
npm run verify   # static contract check + all tests
npm test         # 305 tests, no DSH install required
npm run check    # contract check only
```

Four layers, none needing DSH: pure logic (parsers, preset chain, cache/throttle), host integration (stubs for `@deepseek-ai/*`, running the real `apply()`), a static contract check, and **browser-half render tests** (real `client.js` loaded with a minimal React stub and rendered across its states).

That last layer earns its keep: a `useMemo` referencing a `const` declared below it is a runtime scope error — invisible to `node --check` and to the contract check, but it crashes the component and makes the reado

plugins.description: MCP 服务安全：审计 MCP 配置里的未锁定远端包、明文端点、可执行本地服务。
plugins.readme_text: # @deepwhale-cn/dsh-mcp-audit [![dshfind 收录](https://dshfind.com/api/badge/feely0208/dsh-mcp-audit?lang=zh)](https://dshfind.com/zh/plugins/feely0208/dsh-mcp-audit) [![Listed on dsh-plugin.org](https://dsh-plugin.org/badges/listed.svg)](https://dsh-plugin.org/plugins/feely0208/dsh-mcp-audit) **MCP 安全**：未锁定的远端包、明文端点、可执行本地服务 —— MCP 是 agent 的新攻击面。 **关键词**：MCP 安全 · MCP 审计 · 模型上下文协议 · MCP 配置 · 未锁版本 · MCP 投毒 · MCP 服务 **Keywords**: MCP security · MCP audit · model context protocol · server security · MCP supply chain **MCP 服务安全** —— 审计 MCP 配置里的未锁定远端包、明文端点、可执行本地服务。 ## 不装它会怎样 你的 MCP 配置写的是： ```json "filesystem": { "command": "npx", "args": ["-y", "@modelcontextprotocol/server-filesystem"] } ``` 看起来很正常。但 `npx -y` 意味着**每次启动都拉最新版** —— 上游某个版本被投毒，你开着 agent 用文件工具的那一刻就在执行它。 而且你**没有任何版本记录可以回滚**。 锁成 `@2024.11.0` 就能防住这一类。 ## 它查什么 | 级别 | 内容 | |---|---| | 🔴 高 | `npx -y` 未锁版本 · 明文 http:// 端点 | | 🟡 中 | 指向本地可执行文件/脚本 | | 🟢 低 | 仓库里找不到 MCP 配置 | ## 为什么 MCP 特别值得查 **MCP 服务拿到的权限通常比一般插件大得多** —— 能读写文件、执行工具、访问账号。 而它的配置常常散落在个人机器上、不在版本控制里、没人审查过。 **给 agent 装 MCP 服务，等于给它开门。** ## 安装 ```bash dsh plugin --profile web add @deepwhale-cn/dsh-mcp-audit # 或纯 CLI npx plugins.description: Metadata-only PyPI and MCP Registry distribution for the Qdrant Memory Runtime
plugins.readme_text:
# Qdrant Memory MCP

For shared production deployments, read the [deployment security guide](docs/shared-deployment-security.md). Owner-only database write credentials are required independently of MCP grants. Destination protection and shared doctor are unpublished Runtime additions. Published pins and installation commands remain unchanged.

## One Memory, Multiple Agents — opt-in shared owner

The distribution adds an opt-in single-owner service and stdio bridge. Install Runtime 0.4.0 to use them. See [shared integration guide](integrations/shared/README.md). Private defaults are unchanged. Native Provider automatic shared extraction is deferred.

<!-- mcp-name: io.github.cnkang/qdrant-memory -->

A [WorkBuddy connector](integrations/workbuddy/README.md) and a
[DeepSeek Harness bundle](integrations/dsh/bundle/README.md) reuse this stdio
MCP, the managed launcher and the canonical Skill.

[简体中文](README.zh-CN.md)

Persistent, scoped memory for AI agents through four explicit **stdio MCP** tools.
This repository distributes the existing [Python Runtime](https://github.com/cnkang/hermes-plugin-qdrant-memory).
Its metadata-only wheel contains no Python business implementation. The console
script points directly to `qdrant_memory.standalone:main` and depends on
`hermes-plugin-qdrant-memory[mcp]==0.4.0`.

See [0.1.4 release notes](docs/releases/0.1.4.md) for WorkBuddy assets, SDK compatibility and upgrade guidance.

Before using an exact-version installation command, confirm that version on
the [PyPI release page](https://pypi.org/project/qdrant-memory-mcp/0.2.2/).

**Versions:** MCP distribution 0.2.2 pins Runtime 0.4.0, which supports MCP
Python SDK 1.x and 2.x (`mcp>=1.30,<3`). The four scoped tools and stdio
launch arguments are the same for both SDK majors. It retains the fix for explicit
writes of distinct, highly similar texts without an LLM. The commands below use
these exact versions. Release
artifacts are available through the [distribution PyPI page](https://pypi.org/project/qdrant-memory-mcp/)
and [Runtime PyPI page](https://pypi.org/project/hermes-plugin-qdrant-memory/).
See [release checklist](docs/publishing.md) for the publishing sequence.

Runtime, [optional Agent Skill](https://github.com/cnkang/skills/tree/main/qdrant-memory)
and MCP distribution versions are independent. The Skill is usage guidance,
not a runtime dependency. Hermes retains its native MemoryProvider, automatic
extraction and prefetch. Ordinary MCP performs only explicitly requested memory
operations. It does not automatically extract every conversation turn.

## Install and initialize

For the shortest currently supported local setup, follow the
[Ollama quickstart](docs/quickstart.md) ([中文](docs/quickstart.zh-CN.md)).
It covers an existing model, installing a missing model, a separate WorkBuddy
profile, connection settings and a first save/search check. No Qdrant server,
Docker, cloud account or embedding API key is needed for that local path.
Python/uv and one-time profile configuration are still required for this
direct route. The managed WorkBuddy connector and DSH bundle prepare those
dependencies from Node.js instead.

Requires Python 3.11+ and either [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/) or a Python
virtual environment. You must configure storage and an embedding service.
For the example below, run Ollama and install `qwen3-embedding:4b` yourself.

Create an operator-owned profile directory and save `qdrant-memory.json` inside:

```json
{
  "schema_version": 1,
  "scope": {"user_id": "my-user", "agent_id": "my-agent"},
  "qdrant": {"mode": "embedded", "collection": "qdrant_memory"},
  "embedding": {
    "mode": "plugin", "provider": "ollama", "model": "qwen3-embedding:4b",
    "base_url": "http://127.0.0.1:11434", "dimensions": 2560, "distance": "Cosine"
  }
}
```

Initialize, then launch (replace `/path/to/profile` with your absolute path):

```bash
uvx --from qdrant-memory-mcp==0.2.2 qdrant-memory-mcp --home /path/to/profile init
uvx --from qdrant-memory-mcp==0.2.2 qdrant-memory-mcp --home /path/to/profile mcp
```

The command without `--home` uses `~/.qdrant-memory`, independent of Hermes.
Configure and initialize that directory before letting a Registry client launch
`uvx --from qdrant-memory-mcp==0.2.2 qdrant-memory-mcp mcp`.
The executable name matches the package name.
The Registry's positional `mcp` selects protocol mode. Its optional named
`--home` precedes `mcp` when a client supplies a custom profile.

Alternatively:

```bash
python3 -m venv .venv
.venv/bin/python -m pip install qdrant-memory-mcp==0.2.2
.venv/bin/qdrant-memory-mcp --home /path/to/profile init
.venv/bin/qdrant-memory-mcp --home /path/to/profile mcp
```

On Windows use `.venv\Scripts\python.exe` and
`.venv\Scripts\qdrant-memory-mcp.exe`.

Qdrant embedded, self-hosted server and Cloud, plus Ollama and OpenAI-compatible
embeddings, are configured in the Runtime's [configuration reference](https://github.com/cnkang/hermes-plugin-qdrant-memory/blob/main/docs/configuration.md).
Keep credentials in operator environment variables (`QDRANT_API_KEY`,
`EMBEDDING_API_KEY`, or configured names). Never commit their values.
Initialization against an existing collection requires explicit operator choice.
Do not use a production destination for a first test.

## Connect a client

Codex `config.toml` example:

```toml
[mcp_servers.qdrant_memory]
command = "uvx"
args = ["--from", "qdrant-memory-mcp==0.2.2", "qdrant-memory-mcp", "--home", "/path/to/profile", "mcp"]
```

OpenCode `opencode.json` example:

```json
{
  "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json",
  "mcp": {
    "qdrant_memory": {
      "type": "local",
      "command": ["uvx", "--from", "qdrant-memory-mcp==0.2.2", "qdrant-memory-mcp", "--home", "/path/to/profile", "mcp"],
      "enabled": true
    }
  }
}
```

Pi needs a separately installed MCP client/extension. In that extension, use
`command: uvx` and the same argument list. No built-in Pi MCP support or universal
extension config format is claimed. These are configuration examples. This
distribution's acceptance tests use the official Python MCP SDK, not live agent
applications. See the Runtime's [client evidence and limits](https://github.com/cnkang/hermes-plugin-qdrant-memory/blob/main/docs/mcp.md).

## Tools and boundaries

| Tool | Input | Result |
|---|---|---|
| `qdrant_memory_search` | `query`, optional `category` | Scoped memories with IDs, scores and provenance |
| `qdrant_memory_add` | `text` | Durable memory ID |
| `qdrant_memory_update` | exact `id`, replacement `text` | Scoped replacement |
| `qdrant_memory_delete` | exact `id` | Scoped deletion |

Scope is fixed by the operator's profile (`user_id`, `agent_id`). Model inputs
and MCP client identity cannot override it. Knowing an ID does not grant access.
Migration, export, reset and bulk deletion remain trusted operator CLI commands.
See [standalone maintenance](https://github.com/cnkang/hermes-plugin-qdrant-memory/blob/main/docs/standalone.md).
No resources or prompts are advertised. This is a local subprocess, with no
public HTTP/SSE listener or remote authentication service. Stdout is reserved
for protocol messages, with sanitized diagnostics on stderr.

Data flows from client → Runtime → embedding provider → Qdrant and the local
SQLite ledger. With local Ollama and embedded Qdrant, memory processing stays
local. Cloud embedding receives memory/query text, and cloud Qdrant receives
vectors and stored payloads. The client/model may also receive recalled text.
The operator must authorize retention and access and protect the profile files.

One writer lease coordinates a profile/destination. Do not overlap MCP, CLI
or Hermes processes writing to it. Separate profiles or machines do not provide
a distributed lock. This package does not support uncoordinated multiprocess
writes, auto-extraction, an HTTP transport, or implicit credential discovery
from Hermes. It preserves the Runtime's ledger, IDs and recovery semantics.

## Verification and development

CI builds wheel/sdist, checks metadata and ownership marker. It runs installed
protocol tests with temporary profiles, embedded Qdrant and a deterministic
loopback e
